title.zh: 卷八十 列傳第六十八: 外戚
title.en: Volume 80 Biographies 68: Families of Imperial Consorts
title.raw: 卷八十 列傳第六十八: 外戚 Volume 80 Biographies 68: Families of Imperial Consorts

sentences.zh: 夫左賢右戚，尚德尊功，有國者所以禦天下也。

translations.literal: As for placing the worthy on the left and consort kin on the right, honoring virtue and respecting merit—these are how one who holds a state governs all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler governs the realm by placing worthy men on the left and consort kin on the right, honoring virtue and esteeming merit.

sentences.zh: 殷肇王基，不藉莘氏為佐；

translations.literal: The Yin laid the royal foundation without taking the Shen clan as assistants;
translations.idiomatic: When the Yin first laid their royal foundation, they did not rely on the Shen clan as helpers.

sentences.zh: 周成王業，未聞姒姓為輔。

translations.literal: For King Cheng of Zhou's enterprise, one never heard of the Si surname serving as helpers.
translations.idiomatic: King Cheng of Zhou's achievement owed nothing to Si-clan aides either.

sentences.zh: 然曆觀累代外戚之家，乘母后之權以取高位厚秩者，多矣！

translations.literal: Yet surveying successive generations, among families of imperial consorts, those who rode the empress dowager's power to obtain high office and rich stipends were many!
translations.idiomatic: Yet down through the ages, countless consort families seized lofty posts and lavish salaries by exploiting the empress dowager's authority.

sentences.zh: 而鮮能有克終之美，必罹顛覆之患，何哉？

translations.literal: Yet few could achieve the beauty of a good end; they invariably met the calamity of overthrow—why?
translations.idiomatic: Yet few ever finished well; most met ruin. Why?

sentences.zh: 皆由乎居上不以至公任物，在下徒用私寵要榮。

translations.literal: All because those above did not employ the utmost fairness in assigning duties, while those below relied solely on private favor to seek glory.
translations.idiomatic: Because those above failed to appoint people with perfect fairness, and those below pursued rank through private favor alone.

sentences.zh: 繭犢引大車，升質任厚棟，無德而尊，不知紀極，忽于滿盈之戒，罔念高危之咎。

translations.literal: Like a silkworm or calf drawing a great carriage, like inferior timber raised as a thick ridgepole—honored without virtue, ignorant of limits, heedless of the warning when full, unmindful of the blame of standing high.
translations.idiomatic: They were like silkworms pulling great carts, or crude timber propped up as main beams—ennobled without merit, heedless of limits, forgetting the warning against overfullness and the peril of lofty place.

sentences.zh: 故鬼瞰其室，憂必及之，所以殺身傾族相繼於西京也。

translations.literal: Therefore ghosts peered into their houses; misfortune was bound to reach them—hence self-destruction and clan ruin followed one after another in the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Spirits looked into their homes, and ruin was inevitable—which is why loss of life and destruction of clans recurred one after another in the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 夫誠著艱難，功宣社稷，不以謙沖自牧，未免顛蹶之禍；

translations.literal: When sincerity was shown in hardship and merit served the altars of state, yet one did not restrain oneself with modest humility, one could not escape the calamity of a fall;
translations.idiomatic: Even those who proved loyal through hardship and whose deeds upheld the state, if they did not cultivate modest restraint, still could not escape disaster;

sentences.zh: 而況道不足以濟時，仁不足以利物，自矜於己，以富貴驕人者乎！

translations.literal: How much more those whose Way was insufficient to aid the age, whose benevolence was insufficient to benefit things, who prided themselves and used wealth and honor to look down on others!
translations.idiomatic: How much less those whose virtue could not save the times, whose kindness could not help others, yet who flaunted themselves and lorded their wealth and rank over everyone!

sentences.zh: 魏道武初，賀訥有部眾之業，翼成皇祚，其餘或以勞勤，或緣恩澤。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Daowu of Wei, He Ne had the enterprise of tribal followers and aided in establishing the imperial throne; the rest either through labor or through grace of favor.
translations.idiomatic: In the early reign of Emperor Daowu of Wei, He Ne commanded tribal forces and helped found the dynasty; the others owed their standing to hard service or imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 齊氏后妃之族，多自保全。

translations.literal: The consort families of the Qi house for the most part preserved themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the Northern Qi empresses' kin managed to survive intact.

sentences.zh: 胡長仁以譖訴貽禍，斛律光以地勢被戮，俱非女謁盛衰之所致也。

translations.literal: Hu Changren met disaster through slander and accusation; Hulu Guang was executed on account of territorial power—neither was caused by the rise and fall of women's influence at court.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Changren was destroyed by false accusations, and Hulu Guang was killed because of his territorial base—neither case stemmed from consort power waxing or waning.

sentences.zh: 婁昭自以佐命之功，崇其名器，且霸業權輿，時方同德，陵暴之釁，因茲而起。

translations.literal: Lou Zhao, relying on his merit in aiding the founding mandate, exalted his titles and offices; moreover, when the hegemonic enterprise was in its infancy and the times called for united purpose, the seeds of arrogance and oppression arose from this.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Zhao, crediting himself with helping establish the dynasty, inflated his rank and honors; at a time when the state was still being built and unity was needed, the impulse toward domineering conduct took root here.

sentences.zh: 其靖德、昭訓二門，並良家遺孽，守死無暇，固不足涉言。

translations.literal: The Jingde and Zhaoxun branches were both remnants of good families, clinging to death with no leisure for anything else—they hardly merit discussion.
translations.idiomatic: The Jingde and Zhaoxun lines were both scions of respectable houses, too busy merely surviving to matter here.

sentences.zh: 又子非繼世，權難妄假。

translations.literal: Moreover, when sons were not heirs to the line, authority could not be rashly lent.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, when a man was not the legitimate heir, power could not be casually bestowed.

sentences.zh: 昭信非惟素門履道，訖構廢辱，威望之地，自致無由。

translations.literal: Zhaoxin not only came from a plain household and walked the proper path, yet ended in disgrace and ruin; in a place of prestige and authority, he had no means to advance himself.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoxin was from a humble house and kept to the right path, yet still met disgrace and downfall; in a position of power and renown, he could not secure his own rise.

sentences.zh: 有周禦曆，後門初無與政，既而末跡竊權，竟移鼎璽，斯乃西漢覆車之轍，魏文所以深誡。

translations.literal: When Northern Zhou held the mandate, the empress's kin at first took no part in government; later, in its final phase, they usurped power and at last shifted the imperial seals—this was the same track as the overturned chariot of Western Han, and why Emperor Wen of Wei issued stern warnings.
translations.idiomatic: Under Northern Zhou, consort kin initially stayed out of politics; in the dynasty's last days they seized power and finally moved the throne—repeating Western Han's fatal precedent, which is why Emperor Wen of Wei warned so sternly against it.

sentences.zh: 隋文潛躍之初，獻後便相推轂；

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Wen of Sui's hidden rise, Empress Xian already pushed the wheel for him;
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui was still rising in obscurity, Empress Xian was already driving his cause forward;

sentences.zh: 煬帝大橫方兆，蕭妃密勿經綸。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang's great mandate was just appearing, Consort Xiao took part in secret state planning.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang's imperial destiny was taking shape, Consort Xiao shared closely in statecraft behind the scenes.

sentences.zh: 是以恩禮綢繆，始終不易。

translations.literal: Therefore favor and ritual were intimate, and from beginning to end they did not change.
translations.idiomatic: Their bond of favor and courtesy remained close and unchanging from start to finish.

sentences.zh: 然外內親戚，莫預朝權，昆弟在位，亦無殊寵。

translations.literal: Yet consort kin inside and outside the palace took no part in court power; brothers in office likewise received no special favor.
translations.idiomatic: Yet neither inner nor outer consort relatives held court power, and brothers who served in office received no extraordinary indulgence.

sentences.zh: 至於居擅玉堂，家稱金穴，暉光戚裏，熏灼四方，將三司以比儀，命五侯而同拜者，終始一代，寂無聞焉。

translations.literal: As for monopolizing the jade hall, households called gold caves, glory shining through the empress's kin, blazing on all four sides, treating the Three Excellencies as peers, and ordering the Five Marquises to bow alike—through a whole generation, not a whisper was heard of such things.
translations.idiomatic: No one in that entire age monopolized the court like a jade hall, amassed wealth like a house of gold, blazed with empress-kin splendor across the realm, ranked alongside the Three Excellencies, or had the Five Marquises bow as equals.

sentences.zh: 考之前王，可謂矯其弊矣。

translations.literal: Considering the former kings, one may say they corrected this abuse.
translations.idiomatic: Measured against earlier rulers, the Sui emperors may be said to have corrected this abuse.

sentences.zh: 故雖時經擾攘，無有陷於不義，市朝遷貿，而皆得以保全。

translations.literal: Therefore, although the times passed through turmoil, none fell into unrighteousness; as markets and courts shifted, all were able to preserve themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Thus even through turbulent times, none were drawn into injustice; as power changed hands in court and market, they all survived.

sentences.zh: 比夫憑藉寵私，階緣恩澤，乘其非據，旋就顛隕者，豈可同日而言哉！

translations.literal: Compared with those who relied on private favor, climbed by grace of favor, seized what was not theirs, and swiftly met ruin—how can they be spoken of on the same day!
translations.idiomatic: Compared with those who traded on private favor, rode imperial grace to power, seized what they had no right to hold, and quickly fell—there is no comparison!

sentences.zh: 此所謂愛之以禮者也。

translations.literal: This is what is meant by loving them through ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: This is what is meant by loving them with proper restraint.

sentences.zh: 案外戚，《魏書》有賀訥、劉羅辰、姚黃眉、杜超、賀迷、閭毗、馮熙、李峻、李惠、高肇、于勁、胡國珍、李延實，《齊書》有趙猛、婁睿、爾硃文暢、鄭仲禮、李祖升、元蠻、胡長仁，《周書》不立此篇，《隋書》有獨孤羅、蕭巋。

translations.literal: Examining consort kin: the Book of Wei has He Ne, Liu Luochen, Yao Huangmei, Du Chao, He Mi, Lü Pi, Feng Xi, Li Jun, Li Hui, Gao Zhao, Yu Jin, Hu Guozhen, and Li Yanshi; the Book of Qi has Zhao Meng, Lou Rui, Erzhu Wenchang, Zheng Zhongli, Li Zusheng, Yuan Man, and Hu Changren; the Book of Zhou does not establish this section; the Book of Sui has Dugu Luo and Xiao Kui.
translations.idiomatic: On consort families: the Book of Wei includes He Ne, Liu Luochen, Yao Huangmei, Du Chao, He Mi, Lü Pi, Feng Xi, Li Jun, Li Hui, Gao Zhao, Yu Jin, Hu Guozhen, and Li Yanshi; the Book of Qi includes Zhao Meng, Lou Rui, Erzhu Wenchang, Zheng Zhongli, Li Zusheng, Yuan Man, and Hu Changren; the Book of Zhou has no such chapter; the Book of Sui has Dugu Luo and Xiao Kui.

sentences.zh: 今以劉羅辰、李峻、于勁、李延實、婁睿、爾硃文暢、鄭仲禮、李祖升、元蠻、獨孤羅、蕭巋各附其家傳，其餘併入此篇。

translations.literal: Now Liu Luochen, Li Jun, Yu Jin, Li Yanshi, Lou Rui, Erzhu Wenchang, Zheng Zhongli, Li Zusheng, Yuan Man, Dugu Luo, and Xiao Kui are each attached to their family biographies; the rest are combined in this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Luochen, Li Jun, Yu Jin, Li Yanshi, Lou Rui, Erzhu Wenchang, Zheng Zhongli, Li Zusheng, Yuan Man, Dugu Luo, and Xiao Kui are now placed in their respective family accounts; the remainder are gathered in this chapter.

sentences.zh: 又檢楊騰、乙弗繪附之魏末，以備《外戚傳》。

translations.literal: Yang Teng and Yifu Hui are also appended at the end of Wei, to complete the Consort Kin Biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Teng and Yifu Hui are likewise appended at the close of the Wei section to round out the Consort Kin Biographies.

sentences.zh: 賀訥姚黃眉杜超賀迷閭毗馮熙李惠高肇胡國珍從曾孫長粲楊騰乙弗繪趙猛胡長仁隋文帝外家呂氏

translations.literal: He Ne, Yao Huangmei, Du Chao, He Mi, Lü Pi, Feng Xi, Li Hui, Gao Zhao, Hu Guozhen, his great-grandson Chang Can, Yang Teng, Yifu Hui, Zhao Meng, Hu Changren, and the Lü clan, maternal kin of Emperor Wen of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: He Ne; Yao Huangmei; Du Chao; He Mi; Lü Pi; Feng Xi; Li Hui; Gao Zhao; Hu Guozhen; his great-grandson Chang Can; Yang Teng; Yifu Hui; Zhao Meng; Hu Changren; and the Lü clan, maternal relatives of Emperor Wen of Sui.

sentences.zh: 賀訥，代人，魏道武皇帝之舅，獻明後之兄也。

translations.literal: He Ne was a man of Dai, maternal uncle of Emperor Daowu of Wei and elder brother of Empress Xianming.
translations.idiomatic: He Ne was from Dai, maternal uncle to Emperor Daowu of Wei and elder brother of Empress Xianming.

sentences.zh: 其先世為君長。

translations.literal: His forebears for generations were tribal chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors had been tribal chiefs for generations.

sentences.zh: 祖紇，尚平文女。

translations.literal: His grandfather He was married to a daughter of Emperor Pingwen.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather He married a daughter of Emperor Pingwen.

sentences.zh: 父野幹，尚昭成女遼西公主。

translations.literal: His father Yegan was married to the Princess of Liaoxi, daughter of Emperor Zhaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yegan married the Princess of Liaoxi, daughter of Emperor Zhaocheng.

sentences.zh: 昭成崩，諸部乖亂，獻明後與道武及衛、秦二王依訥。

translations.literal: When Zhaocheng died, the tribes fell into disorder; Empress Xianming, Daowu, and the Princes of Wei and Qin relied on Ne.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhaocheng's death the tribes fell into chaos; Empress Xianming, Daowu, and the Princes of Wei and Qin took refuge with Ne.

sentences.zh: 會苻堅使劉庫仁分攝國事，道武還居獨孤。

translations.literal: At that time Fu Jian sent Liu Kuren to share in governing the state; Daowu returned to dwell at Dugu.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian then sent Liu Kuren to share control of the realm, and Daowu withdrew to Dugu.

sentences.zh: 訥總攝東部為大人，遷居大寧，行其恩信，眾多歸之，侔於庫仁。

translations.literal: Ne took overall charge of the eastern tribes as a great chief, moved his residence to Daning, practiced kindness and trust, and many came to join him, rivaling Kuren.
translations.idiomatic: Ne became great chief over the eastern tribes, moved to Daning, won people through kindness and trust, and drew so many followers that he rivaled Kuren.

sentences.zh: 苻堅假訥鷹揚將軍。

translations.literal: Fu Jian made Ne acting General of Soaring Hawk.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian appointed Ne acting General of Soaring Hawk.

sentences.zh: 後劉顯謀逆，道武輕騎歸訥，訥驚拜曰：「官家復國，當念老臣。」

translations.literal: Later Liu Xian plotted rebellion; Daowu came with a light escort to Ne. Ne bowed in alarm and said, "When the ruler restores the state, he should remember this old servant.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Xian rebelled, Daowu rode lightly to Ne. Ne bowed in alarm and said, "When Your Majesty restores the realm, remember this old servant.

sentences.zh: 帝笑答曰「誠如舅言，要不亡也。」

translations.literal: The emperor answered with a smile, "Truly as my uncle says—I was not to perish after all."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor smiled and replied, "Just as you say, Uncle—I was not destined to die after all."

sentences.zh: 訥中弟染幹粗暴，忌帝，常圖為逆。

translations.literal: Ne's younger brother Rangan was brutal and resented the emperor, often plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Ne's younger brother Rangan was violent and hostile to the emperor and often plotted treason.

sentences.zh: 每為皇姑遼西公主擁護，故染幹不得肆共禍心。

translations.literal: Each time the imperial aunt, the Princess of Liaoxi, shielded him, so Rangan could not fully carry out his wicked intent.
translations.idiomatic: Each time the imperial aunt, the Princess of Liaoxi, protected Daowu, so Rangan could not carry out his designs.

sentences.zh: 諸部大人請訥兄弟，求舉道武為主，染幹不從。

translations.literal: The great chiefs of the tribes asked Ne and his brothers to install Daowu as lord; Rangan would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: The tribal chiefs asked Ne and his brothers to raise Daowu as ruler; Rangan refused.

sentences.zh: 遂與諸大人勸進，道武登代王位于牛川。

translations.literal: Thereupon, together with the great chiefs, they urged him forward, and Daowu ascended the throne of Prince of Dai at Niuchuan.
translations.idiomatic: They then joined the great chiefs in urging him forward, and Daowu took the throne of Prince of Dai at Niuchuan.

sentences.zh: 及帝討吐突鄰部，訥兄弟遂懷異圖，率諸部救之。

translations.literal: When the emperor campaigned against the Tujiuli tribe, Ne and his brothers harbored a different design and led the tribes to rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor attacked the Tujiuli tribe, Ne and his brothers turned disloyal and led the tribes to their rescue.

sentences.zh: 帝擊之，大潰，訥西遁。

translations.literal: The emperor struck them and routed them utterly; Ne fled west.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor defeated them utterly and Ne fled west.

sentences.zh: 衛辰遣子直力鞮征訥，告急請降。

translations.literal: Weichen sent his son Zhilidi to campaign against Ne; Ne reported urgency and asked to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Weichen sent his son Zhilidi against Ne, who in distress appealed for surrender.

sentences.zh: 道武簡精騎二十萬救之，遂徙訥部落及諸弟，處之東界。

translations.literal: Daowu selected two hundred thousand elite horsemen to rescue him, then moved Ne's tribe and his brothers and settled them on the eastern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Daowu marched two hundred thousand picked horsemen to his aid, then relocated Ne's tribe and his brothers to the eastern border.

sentences.zh: 訥又通于慕容垂，垂以訥為歸善王。

translations.literal: Ne also communicated with Murong Chui, who made Ne Prince of Returning Goodness.
translations.idiomatic: Ne also allied with Murong Chui, who made him Prince of Returning Goodness.

sentences.zh: 染幹謀殺訥而代立，訥遂與染幹相攻。

translations.literal: Rangan plotted to kill Ne and take his place; Ne then fought Rangan.
translations.idiomatic: Rangan plotted to kill Ne and replace him, and Ne fought back.

sentences.zh: 垂遣子麟討之，敗染幹于牛都，破訥於赤城。

translations.literal: Chui sent his son Lin to attack them, defeating Rangan at Niudu and breaking Ne at Chicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Chui sent his son Lin against them, defeating Rangan at Niudu and Ne at Chicheng.

sentences.zh: 道武遣師救訥，麟乃引退。

translations.literal: Daowu sent troops to rescue Ne, and Lin then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Daowu sent troops to rescue Ne, and Lin withdrew.

sentences.zh: 訥從道武平中原，拜安遠將軍。

translations.literal: Ne followed Daowu in pacifying the Central Plains and was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distant.
translations.idiomatic: Ne followed Daowu in conquering the Central Plains and was made General Who Pacifies the Distant.

sentences.zh: 其後離散諸部，分土定居，不聽遷徙。

translations.literal: Afterward the tribes were dispersed, given land and settled, and not permitted to migrate.
translations.idiomatic: Later the tribes were broken up, assigned land, and forbidden to migrate.

sentences.zh: 其君長大人，皆同編戶。

translations.literal: Their chiefs and great men were all registered like common households.
translations.idiomatic: Their chiefs and elders were all enrolled as ordinary households.

sentences.zh: 訥以元舅，甚見尊重，然無統領，以壽終於家。

translations.literal: Because Ne was the emperor's senior maternal uncle, he was greatly respected, yet he had no command and died at home of old age.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor's chief maternal uncle, Ne was greatly honored but held no command and died at home in old age.

sentences.zh: 訥弟盧，亦從平中原，以功賜爵遼西公。

translations.literal: Ne's younger brother Lu also followed in pacifying the Central Plains and, for merit, was granted the title Duke of Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: Ne's younger brother Lu also helped pacify the Central Plains and was enfeoffed Duke of Liaoxi for his service.

sentences.zh: 帝遣盧會衛王儀伐鄴，而盧自以帝之季舅，不肯受儀節度。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Lu to join Prince Wei of the Guard in attacking Ye, but Lu, considering himself the emperor's junior maternal uncle, refused to accept the prince's command.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Lu to join Prince Wei of the Guard against Ye, but Lu, as the emperor's junior maternal uncle, refused to obey the prince.

sentences.zh: 帝遣使切責之，盧遂忿恨，與儀司馬丁建構成其嫌，彌加猜忌。

translations.literal: The emperor sent envoys to rebuke him sternly; Lu then grew resentful, and together with the prince's marshal Ding Jian fanned their mutual dislike, adding to suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sharply rebuked him; Lu grew angry, and with the prince's marshal Ding Jian he deepened their mutual distrust.

sentences.zh: 會道武敕儀去鄴，盧亦引歸。

translations.literal: When Daowu ordered the prince to leave Ye, Lu also withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Daowu ordered the prince away from Ye, Lu withdrew as well.

sentences.zh: 道武以盧為廣川太守。

translations.literal: Daowu made Lu Administrator of Guangchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Daowu appointed Lu Administrator of Guangchuan.

sentences.zh: 盧性雄豪，恥居冀州刺史王輔下，襲殺輔，奔慕容德。

translations.literal: Lu was by nature bold and overbearing; he was shamed to stand below Wang Fu, Governor of Jizhou, attacked and killed Fu, and fled to Murong De.
translations.idiomatic: Lu was proud and violent, ashamed to rank below Jizhou governor Wang Fu; he killed Fu and fled to Murong De.

sentences.zh: 德以為并州刺史、廣甯王。

translations.literal: De made him Governor of Bingzhou and Prince of Guangning.
translations.idiomatic: De made him Governor of Bingzhou and Prince of Guangning.

sentences.zh: 廣固敗，盧亦沒。

translations.literal: When Guanggu fell, Lu was also captured.
translations.idiomatic: When Guanggu fell, Lu was captured as well.

sentences.zh: 訥從父弟悅。

translations.literal: Ne's paternal cousin Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Ne's paternal cousin Yue.

sentences.zh: 初，道武居賀蘭部下，人情未甚附，唯悅舉部隨從。

translations.literal: At first, when Daowu dwelt among the Helan tribe, men's hearts were not much attached to him; only Yue led his tribe to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, when Daowu lived among the Helan, few were loyal to him; only Yue brought his tribe to follow.

sentences.zh: 又密為帝祈禱天神，請成大業，出於誠至。

translations.literal: He also secretly prayed to Heaven for the emperor, asking that the great enterprise be accomplished—this came from utmost sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: He also secretly prayed to Heaven on the emperor's behalf for success, out of pure devotion.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉之，甚見寵待。

translations.literal: The emperor praised this and greatly favored him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor valued this and treated him with exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 後平中原，以功賜爵钜鹿侯，進爵北新，卒。

translations.literal: Later, when the Central Plains were pacified, he was granted the title Marquis of Julu for merit, advanced to Beixin, and died.
translations.idiomatic: After the Central Plains were pacified he was made Marquis of Julu, then advanced to Beixin, and died.

sentences.zh: 子泥襲爵，後降為肥如侯。

translations.literal: His son Ni inherited the title and was later reduced to Marquis of Feiru.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ni inherited the title and was later reduced to Marquis of Feiru.

sentences.zh: 道武崩，京師草草，泥出，舉烽於安陽城北，賀蘭部人皆往赴之。

translations.literal: When Daowu died, the capital was in turmoil; Ni went out and raised beacon fires north of Anyang city, and all the Helan tribesmen went to join him.
translations.idiomatic: At Daowu's death the capital was unsettled; Ni raised beacon fires north of Anyang, and Helan tribesmen flocked to him.

sentences.zh: 明元即位，乃罷。

translations.literal: When Mingyuan took the throne, this ceased.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingyuan succeeded, the movement ended.

sentences.zh: 詔泥與元渾等八人拾遺左右。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Ni, together with Yuan Hun and seven others, to remonstrate at the ruler's side.
translations.idiomatic: Ni was ordered, with Yuan Hun and seven others, to advise the throne at close hand.

sentences.zh: 與北新侯安同持節行並、定二州，劾奏并州刺史元六頭等，皆伏罪，州郡肅然。

translations.literal: Together with Beixin Marquis An Tong he bore credentials and inspected Bing and Ding provinces, impeaching Bingzhou governor Yuan Liutou and others; all were found guilty, and the provinces grew orderly.
translations.idiomatic: With Beixin Marquis An Tong he inspected Bing and Ding, impeached Bingzhou governor Yuan Liutou and others, secured their convictions, and restored order in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 後從太武征赫連昌，以功進爵為琅邪公，軍國大議，每參豫焉。

translations.literal: Later he followed Emperor Taiwu in campaigning against Helian Chang and, for merit, was advanced to Duke of Langye; on great matters of army and state he took part in deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed Taiwu against Helian Chang, was made Duke of Langye for merit, and joined deliberations on army and state.

sentences.zh: 又征蠕蠕，為別道將，坐逐賊不進，詐增虜，當斬。

translations.literal: Again on campaign against the Rouran, he served as a commander on a separate route; for pursuing the enemy without advancing and falsely inflating captive numbers, he deserved execution.
translations.idiomatic: On another Rouran campaign he commanded a separate column; for failing to pursue the enemy and falsifying captive counts, he was sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 贖為庶人。

translations.literal: He was ransomed to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: He was ransomed down to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 久之，拜光祿勳，為外都大官，復本爵。

translations.literal: After a long while he was appointed Director of the Imperial Household, served as Grand Official of the Outer Court, and recovered his original title.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he was made Director of the Imperial Household and Grand Official of the Outer Court, and regained his former title.

sentences.zh: 卒官，子醜建襲。

translations.literal: He died in office; his son Choujian inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office; his son Choujian succeeded.

sentences.zh: 姚黃眉，姚興之子，明元昭哀皇后之弟也。

translations.literal: Yao Huangmei was a son of Yao Xing and younger brother of Empress Zhaoguangai of Mingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Huangmei was a son of Yao Xing and younger brother of Mingyuan's Empress Zhaoguangai.

sentences.zh: 姚泓滅，黃眉間來歸魏。

translations.literal: When Yao Hong was destroyed, Huangmei came over to Wei by a separate route.
translations.idiomatic: After Yao Hong's fall Huangmei made his way to Wei.

sentences.zh: 明元厚禮待之，賜爵隴西公。

translations.literal: Mingyuan treated him with generous ritual and granted him the title Duke of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Mingyuan received him with great courtesy and enfeoffed him Duke of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 尚陽翟公主，拜附馬都尉，隸戶二百。

translations.literal: He married the Princess of Yangzhai, was appointed Commandant of the Horse Guards, and received two hundred dependent households.
translations.idiomatic: He married the Princess of Yangzhai, became Commandant of the Horse Guards, and received two hundred dependent households.

sentences.zh: 太武即位，遷內都大官，後拜太常卿，卒。

translations.literal: When Taiwu took the throne, he was transferred to Grand Official of the Inner Court, later appointed Minister of Ceremonies, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taiwu he became Grand Official of the Inner Court, later Minister of Ceremonies, and died.

sentences.zh: 贈雍州刺史、隴西王，諡曰獻，陪葬金陵。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Governor of Yongzhou and Prince of Longxi, with the posthumous title Xian, and buried with honor at Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made Governor of Yongzhou and Prince of Longxi, titled Xian, and buried with honor at Jinling.

sentences.zh: 黃眉寬和溫厚，希言得失，太武悼惜之，故贈禮有加。

translations.literal: Huangmei was broad, mild, and warm; he rarely spoke of gain or loss. Taiwu mourned him and therefore added to the posthumous honors.
translations.idiomatic: Huangmei was open, gentle, and temperate, and seldom spoke of advantage or harm. Taiwu grieved for him and added to his funeral honors.

sentences.zh: 杜超，字祖仁，魏郡鄴人，密皇后之兄也。

translations.literal: Du Chao, style Zuren, was a man of Ye in Wei Commandery and elder brother of Empress Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Du Chao, style Zuren, was from Ye in Wei Commandery and elder brother of Empress Mi.

sentences.zh: 少有節操。

translations.literal: From youth he had integrity of conduct.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he showed moral integrity.

sentences.zh: 泰常中，為相州別駕。

translations.literal: In the Taichang era he served as Registrar of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During Taichang he served as Registrar of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 始光中，太武思念舅氏，以超為陽平公，尚南安長公主，拜附馬都尉，位大鴻臚卿，車駕幸其第，賞賜巨萬。

translations.literal: In the Shiguang era, Taiwu, thinking of his maternal kin, made Chao Duke of Yangping, married him to the Princess of Nan'an, appointed him Commandant of the Horse Guards and Grand Minister of the Imperial Clan; the imperial carriage visited his residence and bestowed gifts in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In Shiguang, Taiwu, remembering his mother's kin, made Chao Duke of Yangping, married him to the Princess of Nan'an, appointed him Commandant of the Horse Guards and Grand Minister of the Imperial Clan; the emperor visited his home and lavished tens of thousands in gifts.

sentences.zh: 神抅三年，以超行征南大將軍、太宰，進爵為王，鎮鄴。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shenqi, Chao was made acting General Who Conquers the South and Grand Preceptor, advanced to prince, and stationed at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Shenqi, Chao was made acting General Who Conquers the South and Grand Preceptor, raised to prince, and stationed at Ye.

sentences.zh: 追加超父豹鎮東大將軍、陽平景王，母曰钜鹿惠君。

translations.literal: Chao's father Bao was posthumously made General Who Guards the East and Prince Jing of Yangping; his mother was titled Lady Hui of Julu.
translations.idiomatic: Chao's father Bao was posthumously made General Who Guards the East and Prince Jing of Yangping; his mother was titled Lady Hui of Julu.

sentences.zh: 真君五年，超為帳下所害，太武臨其喪，哀慟者久之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenjun, Chao was killed by his attendants; Taiwu attended his funeral and grieved for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Zhenjun, Chao was killed by his attendants; Taiwu came to the funeral and mourned for a long while.

sentences.zh: 諡曰威王。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Prince Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Prince Wei.

sentences.zh: 長子道生賜爵城陽侯，後為秦州刺史，進爵河東公。

translations.literal: His eldest son Daosheng was granted the title Marquis of Chengyang, later became Governor of Qinzhou, and was advanced to Duke of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Daosheng was made Marquis of Chengyang, later Governor of Qinzhou, then Duke of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 道生弟鳳凰襲爵，加侍中、特進。

translations.literal: Daosheng's younger brother Fenghuang inherited the title and was added as Palace Attendant and Special Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: Daosheng's younger brother Fenghuang inherited the title and was made Palace Attendant and Special Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 太武追思超不已，欲以鳳凰為定州刺史。

translations.literal: Taiwu could not stop thinking of Chao and wished to make Fenghuang Governor of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu still missed Chao and wanted to make Fenghuang Governor of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 鳳凰不願違離闕庭，乃止。

translations.literal: Fenghuang did not wish to leave the court precinct and so the appointment stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Fenghuang did not want to leave court and the appointment was dropped.

sentences.zh: 鳳凰弟道俊賜爵發幹侯，鎮枋頭，除兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Fenghuang's younger brother Daojun was granted the title Marquis of Fagan, stationed at Fangtou, and appointed Governor of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fenghuang's younger brother Daojun was made Marquis of Fagan, stationed at Fangtou, and appointed Governor of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 超既薨，復授超從弟遺侍中、安南將軍、開府、相州刺史，入為內都大官，進爵廣平王。

translations.literal: After Chao died, his younger cousin Yi was again appointed Palace Attendant, General Who Pacifies the South, with an established staff, and Governor of Xiangzhou; he entered court as Grand Official of the Inner Court and was advanced to Prince of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: When Chao died, his younger cousin Yi was made Palace Attendant and General Who Pacifies the South, given an established staff, and named Governor of Xiangzhou; he then became Grand Official of the Inner Court and was raised to Prince of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 遺性忠厚，頻曆州郡，所在著稱。

translations.literal: Yi was by nature loyal and generous; he served repeatedly in provinces and commanderies and won renown wherever he went.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was loyal and steadfast by nature; he held many provincial posts and earned a fine reputation in each.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈太傅，諡曰宣王。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously made Grand Tutor, with the posthumous title Prince Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: On his death he was posthumously made Grand Tutor and titled Prince Xuan.

sentences.zh: 長子元寶，位司空。

translations.literal: His eldest son Yuanbao held the post of Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Yuanbao served as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 元寶弟胤寶，司隸校尉。

translations.literal: Yuanbao's younger brother Yinbao was Commandant of the Metropolitan Region.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanbao's younger brother Yinbao was Commandant of the Metropolitan Region.

sentences.zh: 元寶又進爵京兆王。

translations.literal: Yuanbao was further advanced to Prince of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanbao was further enfeoffed as Prince of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 及歸而父遺喪。

translations.literal: When he returned, his father Yi had died.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he returned, his father Yi was dead.

sentences.zh: 明當入謝，元寶欲以表聞。

translations.literal: The next day he was to enter court to give thanks; Yuanbao wished to report this by memorial.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he was to enter court to give thanks, Yuanbao meant to announce it by memorial.

sentences.zh: 文成未知遺薨，怪其遲，召之。

translations.literal: Wencheng did not yet know that Yi had died; puzzled by the delay, he summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wencheng did not yet know Yi had died; finding the delay strange, he summoned him.

sentences.zh: 元寶將入，時人止之曰：「宜以家憂自辭。」

translations.literal: As Yuanbao was about to enter, people stopped him, saying, "You ought to decline on account of family mourning."
translations.idiomatic: As Yuanbao was about to go in, others urged him: "You should beg off because of your father's death."

sentences.zh: 元寶欲見其寵，不從，遂冒哀而入。

translations.literal: Yuanbao wished to show that he enjoyed favor and did not obey; he entered court while still in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanbao wanted to display imperial favor and refused; he went in while still in mourning.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以謀反伏誅，親從皆斬，唯元寶子世沖逃免。

translations.literal: Before long he was executed for plotting rebellion; his close kin were all beheaded, and only Yuanbao's son Shichong escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was executed for treason; his kin were all put to death, and only Yuanbao's son Shichong escaped.

sentences.zh: 時朝議欲追削超爵位，中書令高允上表理之。

translations.literal: At the time court opinion wished to strip Chao of his titles; Director of the Secretariat Gao Yun submitted a memorial in his defense.
translations.idiomatic: The court then wished to revoke Chao's titles; Director of the Secretariat Gao Yun memorialized in his defense.

sentences.zh: 後兗州故吏汲宗等，以道俊遺惠在人，前從坐爵受誅，委骸土壤，求得收葬。

translations.literal: Later former subordinates of Yanzhou, Ji Zong and others, said that Daojun's kindness to the people remained in memory; though kin who shared guilt had been enfeoffed and executed and their bones lay in the soil, they sought permission to gather and bury them.
translations.idiomatic: Later Ji Zong and other former officials of Yanzhou said Daojun's kindness still lived in people's hearts; though kin implicated in the crime had been enfeoffed and slain and their bones lay in the earth, they asked to collect and bury them.

sentences.zh: 書奏，詔義而聽之。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, an edict approved it out of righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was approved by edict as an act of justice.

sentences.zh: 贈散騎常侍、安南將軍、南康公，諡曰昭。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, General Who Pacifies the South, and Duke of Nankang, with the posthumous title Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, General Who Pacifies the South, and Duke of Nankang, titled Zhao.

sentences.zh: 世沖襲遺公爵。

translations.literal: Shichong inherited Duke Yi's title.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong inherited his grandfather Yi's ducal title.

sentences.zh: 賀迷，代人，太武敬哀皇后之從父也。

translations.literal: He Mi was a man of Dai and maternal uncle of Empress Jing'ai of Emperor Taiwu.
translations.idiomatic: He Mi, a native of Dai, was maternal uncle to Emperor Taiwu's Empress Jing'ai.

sentences.zh: 皇后生景穆。

translations.literal: The empress bore Jingmu.
translations.idiomatic: The empress bore Emperor Jingmu.

sentences.zh: 初，後少孤，父兄近親唯迷，故蒙賜爵長鄉子。

translations.literal: At first, when she was young and orphaned, her only close kin on her father's and brothers' side was Mi; therefore he received the enfeoffment of Marquis of Changxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In her youth she was orphaned, and Mi alone among her father's and brothers' kin remained near; for this he was enfeoffed Marquis of Changxiang.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈光祿大夫、五原公。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Duke of Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On his death he was posthumously made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Duke of Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 閭毗，代人，蠕蠕主大檀之親屬，太武時自其國來降。

translations.literal: Lü Pi was a man of Dai, a kinsman of the Rouran ruler Datan; in the Taiwu era he came from that state and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Pi of Dai was kin to the Rouran ruler Datan; under Taiwu he came from that realm and submitted.

sentences.zh: 毗即恭皇后之兄也。

translations.literal: Pi was elder brother of Empress Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Pi was the elder brother of Empress Gong.

sentences.zh: 後生文成。

translations.literal: The empress bore Wencheng.
translations.idiomatic: The empress bore Emperor Wencheng.

sentences.zh: 文成太安二年，以毗為平北將軍，賜爵河東公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tai'an under Wencheng, Pi was made General Who Pacifies the North and granted the title Duke of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: In Wencheng's second Tai'an year, Pi was made General Who Pacifies the North and enfeoffed Duke of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 弟紇為甯北將軍，賜爵零陵公。

translations.literal: His younger brother He was made General Who Guards the North and granted the title Duke of Lingling.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother He was made General Who Guards the North and enfeoffed Duke of Lingling.

sentences.zh: 其年，並加侍中，進爵為王。

translations.literal: That same year both were added as Palace Attendants and advanced to princely rank.
translations.idiomatic: That year both were also made Palace Attendants and raised to princes.

sentences.zh: 毗，征東將軍，評尚書事；

translations.literal: Pi was General Who Conquers the East and Reviewer of Affairs of the Masters of Writing;
translations.idiomatic: Pi became General Who Conquers the East and Reviewer of Affairs of the Masters of Writing;

sentences.zh: 紇，征西將軍、中都大官。

translations.literal: He was General Who Conquers the West and Grand Official of the Central Court.
translations.idiomatic: He was General Who Conquers the West and Grand Official of the Central Court.

sentences.zh: 自余子弟賜爵為王者二人，公五人，侯六人，子三人，同時受拜，所以隆崇舅氏。

translations.literal: The rest of the sons and younger brothers received enfeoffments as two princes, five dukes, six marquises, and three viscounts, all invested at once—thus to exalt the maternal clan.
translations.idiomatic: Other sons and younger brothers were enfeoffed as two princes, five dukes, six marquises, and three viscounts, all invested together to honor the empress's kin.

sentences.zh: 和平二年，追諡後祖父延襄康公，父辰定襄懿王。

translations.literal: In the second year of Heping, the empress's grandfather Yan was posthumously titled Duke Kang of Xiang, and her father Chen Duke Yi of Dingxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second Heping year the empress's grandfather Yan was posthumously titled Duke Kang of Xiang and her father Chen Duke Yi of Dingxiang.

sentences.zh: 毗薨，贈太尉，追贈毗妻河東王妃。

translations.literal: When Pi died he was posthumously made Grand Commandant, and Pi's wife was posthumously made Princess of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: When Pi died he was posthumously made Grand Commandant, and his wife was posthumously made Princess of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 子惠襲。

translations.literal: His son Hui inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hui inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 紇薨，贈司空。

translations.literal: When He died he was posthumously made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When He died he was posthumously made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 子豆，後賜名莊。

translations.literal: His son Dou was later granted the name Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dou was later granted the name Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 太和中，初立三長，以莊為定戶籍大使，甚有時譽。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era, when the Three Chiefs were first established, Zhuang was made Grand Ambassador for Fixing Household Registers and won great contemporary praise.
translations.idiomatic: During Taihe, when the Three Chiefs were first established, Zhuang was made Grand Ambassador for Fixing Household Registers and earned wide praise.

sentences.zh: 十六年，例降爵。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, by precedent his rank was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year his noble rank was lowered by precedent.

sentences.zh: 後為七兵尚書，卒。

translations.literal: Later he was Minister of the Seven Armies and died.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as Minister of the Seven Armies and died.

sentences.zh: 紇弟染，位外都大官、冀州刺史、江夏公，卒。

translations.literal: He's younger brother Ran held the posts of Grand Official of the Outer Court, Governor of Jizhou, and Duke of Jiangxia, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He's younger brother Ran was Grand Official of the Outer Court, Governor of Jizhou, and Duke of Jiangxia, and died.

sentences.zh: 先是，文成以乳母常氏有保護功，既即位，尊為保太后，後尊為皇太后。

translations.literal: Earlier, because Wencheng's wet-nurse, the Lady Chang, had rendered protective service, after he took the throne he honored her as Dowager Protector, and later as Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, because Wencheng's wet-nurse Lady Chang had protected him, once he reigned he honored her as Dowager Protector and later as Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 興安二年，太后前兄英，字世華，自肥如令超為散騎常侍、鎮軍大將軍，賜爵遼西公；

translations.literal: In the second year of Xing'an, the dowager's elder brother Ying, style Shihua, was promoted from Magistrate of Feiru to Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and General Who Guards the Army, and granted the title Duke of Liaoxi;
translations.idiomatic: In the second Xing'an year the dowager's elder brother Ying, style Shihua, rose from Magistrate of Feiru to Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and General Who Guards the Army and was enfeoffed Duke of Liaoxi;

sentences.zh: 弟喜，鎮軍大將軍、祠曹尚書、帶方公；

translations.literal: his younger brother Xi, General Who Guards the Army, Director of the Directorate of Sacrifices, and Duke of Daifang;
translations.idiomatic: his younger brother Xi, General Who Guards the Army, Director of the Directorate of Sacrifices, and Duke of Daifang;

sentences.zh: 三妹皆封縣君；

translations.literal: all three younger sisters were enfeoffed as Ladies of a district;
translations.idiomatic: all three younger sisters were made Ladies of a district;

sentences.zh: 妹夫王暏為平州刺史，遼東公。

translations.literal: Xi married Wang Zhao, Governor of Pingzhou and Duke of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: their brother-in-law Wang Zhao was Governor of Pingzhou and Duke of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 追贈英祖父苻堅扶風太守亥為鎮西將軍、遼西蘭公；

translations.literal: Ying's grandfather Hai, Fufeng Administrator under Fu Jian, was posthumously made General Who Guards the West and Duke Lan of Liaoxi;
translations.idiomatic: Ying's grandfather Hai, Fufeng Administrator under Fu Jian, was posthumously made General Who Guards the West and Duke Lan of Liaoxi;

sentences.zh: 勃海太守澄為侍中、征東大將軍、太宰、遼西獻王；

translations.literal: Cheng, Administrator of Bohai, was posthumously made Palace Attendant, General Who Conquers the East, Grand Preceptor, and Duke Xian of Liaoxi;
translations.idiomatic: Cheng, Bohai Administrator, was posthumously made Palace Attendant, General Who Conquers the East, Grand Preceptor, and Duke Xian of Liaoxi;

sentences.zh: 英母許氏博陵郡君。

translations.literal: Ying's mother, the Lady Xu, was made Lady of Boling Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Ying's mother Lady Xu was made Lady of Boling Commandery.

sentences.zh: 遣兼太常盧度世持節改葬獻王於遼西，樹碑立廟，置守塚百家。

translations.literal: The Concurrent Minister of Ceremonies Lu Dushi was sent with credentials to reinter Duke Xian in Liaoxi, erect a stele and temple, and assign a hundred households to guard the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Dushi, Concurrent Minister of Ceremonies, was dispatched with credentials to reinter Duke Xian in Liaoxi, set up stele and temple, and assign a hundred tomb-guard households.

sentences.zh: 太安初，英為侍中、征東大將軍、太宰，進爵為王；

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tai'an, Ying was Palace Attendant, General Who Conquers the East, and Grand Preceptor, and advanced to princely rank;
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tai'an, Ying was Palace Attendant, General Who Conquers the East, and Grand Preceptor, and was raised to prince;

sentences.zh: 喜左光祿大夫，改封燕郡；

translations.literal: Xi was made Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and his fief changed to Yan Commandery;
translations.idiomatic: Xi was made Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and his fief changed to Yan Commandery;

sentences.zh: 從兄泰為安東將軍、朝鮮侯；

translations.literal: his cousin Tai was General Who Pacifies the East and Marquis of Chaoxian;
translations.idiomatic: his cousin Tai was General Who Pacifies the East and Marquis of Chaoxian;

sentences.zh: 䐶子伯夫，散騎常侍、選部尚書；

translations.literal: Gu's son Bofu, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Ministry of Personnel;
translations.idiomatic: Gu's son Bofu, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Ministry of Personnel;

sentences.zh: 次子員，金部尚書；

translations.literal: his second son Yuan, Minister of the Ministry of Revenue;
translations.idiomatic: his second son Yuan, Minister of the Ministry of Revenue;

sentences.zh: 喜子振，太子庶子。

translations.literal: Xi's son Zhen, Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's son Zhen, Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 三年，英領太師，評尚書事，內都大官、伏寶泰等州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year, Ying held the post of Grand Preceptor, reviewed affairs of the Masters of Writing, and was Grand Official of the Inner Court and regional inspector of Fubao, Tai, and other provinces.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Ying was Grand Preceptor, reviewed Masters of Writing affairs, and served as Grand Official of the Inner Court and regional inspector over Fubao, Tai, and other provinces.

sentences.zh: 五年，詔乙太后母宋氏為遼西王太妃。

translations.literal: In the fifth year an edict made Empress Dowager Yi's mother, the Lady Song, Princess Dowager of Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year an edict made Empress Dowager Yi's mother Lady Song Princess Dowager of Liaoxi.

sentences.zh: 和平元年，喜為洛州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Heping, Xi was Governor of Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first Heping year Xi became Governor of Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 後員與伯夫子禽可共為飛書，誣謗朝政。

translations.literal: Later Yuan, together with Bofu's son Qinke, jointly composed a flying letter slandering court policy.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yuan and Bofu's son Qinke together drafted an anonymous letter defaming court policy.

sentences.zh: 事發，有司執憲，刑及五族。

translations.literal: When the affair came to light, the authorities applied the law, and punishment reached the five clans.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was exposed, the law officers prosecuted it, and punishment extended to five clans.

sentences.zh: 孝文以明太后故，罪止一門。

translations.literal: Because of Empress Dowager Ming, Emperor Xiaowen limited guilt to one house.
translations.idiomatic: For Empress Dowager Ming's sake, Emperor Xiaowen confined punishment to a single household.

sentences.zh: 䐶年老，赦免歸家，恕其孫一人扶養之，經奴婢田宅。

translations.literal: Gu was old in years and was pardoned to return home; one grandson was spared to support him, along with slaves, servants, fields, and houses.
translations.idiomatic: Gu was elderly and pardoned to go home; one grandson was spared to support him, with slaves, servants, land, and dwellings.

sentences.zh: 其家僮入者百人，金錦布帛數萬計，賜尚書已下宿衛已上。

translations.literal: Household slaves seized numbered a hundred persons, with gold, brocade, and silks reckoned in the tens of thousands, which were bestowed on officials from Director of the Secretariat down through palace guards.
translations.idiomatic: Confiscated household slaves numbered a hundred, with gold, brocade, and cloth in the tens of thousands given to officials from Director of the Secretariat down through the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 其女婿及親從在朝，皆免官歸本鄉。

translations.literal: Sons-in-law and kin who held office at court were all dismissed and sent to their native places.
translations.idiomatic: Sons-in-law and kin in court office were all removed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 十一年，孝文、文明太后以文昭太后故，悉出其家前後沒入婦女，以喜子振試守正平郡，卒。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, because of Empress Dowager Wenming, Emperor Xiaowen and Empress Dowager Wenming released all women of the clan previously confiscated; Xi's son Zhen was made acting Administrator of Zhengping Commandery and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, for Empress Dowager Wenming's sake, Emperor Xiaowen and Empress Dowager Wenming released all confiscated women of the clan; Xi's son Zhen was made acting Administrator of Zhengping Commandery and died.

sentences.zh: 馮熙，字晉國，長樂信都人，文明太后之兄也。

translations.literal: Feng Xi, style Jinguo, was a man of Xindu in Changle and elder brother of Empress Dowager Wenming.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Xi, style Jinguo, was from Xindu in Changle and elder brother to Empress Dowager Wenming.

sentences.zh: 祖弘，北燕王。

translations.literal: His grandfather Hong was king of Northern Yan.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Hong was king of Northern Yan.

sentences.zh: 太武平遼海，熙父朗內徙，官至秦雍二州刺史、遼西郡公，坐事誅。

translations.literal: When Taiwu pacified Liaohai, Xi's father Lang was moved inward, reached the posts of Governor of Qin and Yong provinces and Duke of Liaoxi, and was executed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiwu pacified Liaohai, Xi's father Lang was resettled inland, rose to Governor of Qin and Yong and Duke of Liaoxi, and was executed for a crime.

sentences.zh: 文明太后臨朝，追贈假黃鉞、太宰、燕宣王，立廟長安。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Wenming held court, Lang was posthumously given the Golden Axe and Grand Preceptor, titled Prince Xuan of Yan, and a temple was established in Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Wenming ruled, Lang was posthumously given the Golden Axe and Grand Preceptor, titled Prince Xuan of Yan, with a temple in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 熙生於長安，為姚氏魏母所養。

translations.literal: Xi was born in Chang'an and was raised by the Lady Wei, his foster mother.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was born in Chang'an and raised by his foster mother Lady Wei.

sentences.zh: 以叔父樂陵公邈因戰入蠕蠕，魏母攜熙逃避至氐羌中撫育。

translations.literal: Because his uncle, Duke Yao of Leling, had entered Rouran in battle, Lady Wei carried Xi in flight to the Di and Qiang, where she nurtured him.
translations.idiomatic: When his uncle, Duke Yao of Leling, was captured into Rouran in battle, Lady Wei fled with Xi among the Di and Qiang and raised him there.

sentences.zh: 年十二，好弓馬，有勇幹，氐羌皆歸附之。

translations.literal: At twelve he loved bow and horse, showed courage and ability, and Di and Qiang all attached themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he loved archery and horsemanship, showed courage and talent, and Di and Qiang alike rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 魏母惡其如此，將還長安，始就博士學問。

translations.literal: Lady Wei disliked this and was about to return to Chang'an; he then began study under a Erudite.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wei disapproved and took him back to Chang'an, where he first studied under a Erudite.

sentences.zh: 從師受《孝經》、《論語》，好陰陽兵法事。

translations.literal: He followed teachers in the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects, and loved yin-yang and military texts.
translations.idiomatic: He studied the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects and took to yin-yang lore and military strategy.

sentences.zh: 及長，游華陰、河東二郡間。

translations.literal: When grown, he traveled between Huayin and the two commanderies of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: When grown he wandered between Huayin and the two Hedong commanderies.

sentences.zh: 性泛愛，不拘小節，人無士庶，來則納之。

translations.literal: By nature he was broadly affectionate and unconstrained in small matters; whether gentry or commoner, if one came he received him.
translations.idiomatic: He was open-handed and careless of small proprieties; gentry or commoner, all were welcomed if they came.

sentences.zh: 熙姑先入掖庭，為太武左昭儀。

translations.literal: Xi's paternal aunt had earlier entered the Rear Palace as Left Lady of Bright Deportment under Taiwu.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's aunt had earlier entered the rear palace as Taiwu's Left Lady of Bright Deportment.

sentences.zh: 妹為文成帝后，即文明太后也。

translations.literal: His younger sister became Empress of Emperor Wencheng—that is, Empress Dowager Wenming.
translations.idiomatic: His younger sister became Emperor Wencheng's empress, namely Empress Dowager Wenming.

sentences.zh: 使人外訪，知熙所在，征赴京師，拜冠軍將軍，賜爵肥如侯，尚景穆女博陵長公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: Men were sent to seek him abroad; when his whereabouts were known he was summoned to the capital, made General Who Conquers All Challengers, granted the title Marquis of Feiru, married the Princess of Boling, daughter of Jingmu, and appointed Commandant of the Horse Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Agents sought him out; once found he was summoned to the capital, made General Who Conquers All Challengers, enfeoffed Marquis of Feiru, married Princess Boling, daughter of Jingmu, and appointed Commandant of the Horse Guards.

sentences.zh: 出為定州刺史，進爵昌黎王。

translations.literal: He went out as Governor of Dingzhou and was advanced to Prince of Changli.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as Governor of Dingzhou and was raised to Prince of Changli.

sentences.zh: 獻文即位，為太傅，累拜內都大官。

translations.literal: When Xianwen took the throne, he became Grand Tutor and was repeatedly appointed Grand Official of the Inner Court.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xianwen he became Grand Tutor and repeatedly served as Grand Official of the Inner Court.

sentences.zh: 孝文即位，文明太后臨朝，帝乃承旨以熙為侍中、太師、中書監，領秘書事。

translations.literal: When Xiaowen took the throne, Empress Dowager Wenming held court; the emperor then followed her intent and made Xi Palace Attendant, Grand Preceptor, and Director of the Secretariat, overseeing the Imperial Library.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaowen reigned and Empress Dowager Wenming governed, the emperor followed her will and made Xi Palace Attendant, Grand Preceptor, and Director of the Secretariat, in charge of the Imperial Library.

sentences.zh: 熙以頻履師傅，又中宮之寵，為群情所駭，心不自安，乞轉外任。

translations.literal: Because Xi had repeatedly served as imperial tutor and enjoyed the inner palace's favor, the court was alarmed and he felt ill at ease, begging transfer to an outer post.
translations.idiomatic: Having often been imperial tutor and favored within the palace, he alarmed public opinion, grew uneasy, and asked for an outside appointment.

sentences.zh: 文明太后亦以為然，除都督、洛州刺史，侍中、太師如故。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wenming also thought it fitting; he was made Commander-in-Chief and Governor of Luozhou, while Palace Attendant and Grand Preceptor remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager agreed; he was made area commander and Governor of Luozhou, retaining Palace Attendant and Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 洛陽雖經破亂，而舊《三字石經》宛然猶在。

translations.literal: Luoyang, though it had passed through devastation, still had the old Three-Character Stone Classics intact.
translations.idiomatic: Though Luoyang had been ravaged, the old Three-Character Stone Classics still stood intact.

sentences.zh: 至熙與常伯夫相繼為州，廢毀分用，大至頹落。

translations.literal: When Xi and Chang Bofu served as governors in succession, they broke them up for use and they largely collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xi and Chang Bofu, serving as governors in turn, the stones were broken up for reuse and largely ruined.

sentences.zh: 熙為政不能仁厚，而信佛法。

translations.literal: In government Xi could not be benevolent and generous, yet he trusted in Buddhist law.
translations.idiomatic: Xi could not govern with humane breadth, but he trusted in the Buddhist dharma.

sentences.zh: 自出家財在諸州鎮建佛圖精舍，合七十二處。

translations.literal: From his own household wealth he built Buddhist pagodas and monasteries at garrisons and provinces in all, seventy-two sites.
translations.idiomatic: From private means he built pagodas and monasteries at seventy-two garrisons and provinces.

sentences.zh: 寫十六部一切經，延致名德沙門，日與講論，精勤不倦，所費亦不貲。

translations.literal: He copied the complete canon in sixteen sections, invited eminent monks, and debated with them daily, diligent and untiring; the expense too was beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: He had the full canon copied in sixteen parts, invited famous monks for daily disputation, and spent incalculable sums.

sentences.zh: 而營塔寺多在高山秀阜，傷殺人牛。

translations.literal: Yet the pagodas and temples he built stood mostly on lofty hills and fine peaks, harming and killing oxen.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his temples stood on high hills and fine peaks, and oxen were killed in the work.

sentences.zh: 有沙門勸止之，熙曰：「成就後，人唯見佛圖，焉知殺人牛也。」

translations.literal: A monk urged him to stop; Xi said, "When it is finished, people will see only the Buddhist pagoda—how would they know oxen were killed?
translations.idiomatic: A monk tried to dissuade him; Xi said, "When it is done people will see only the pagoda—who will know oxen died?

sentences.zh: 其北芒寺碑文，中書侍郎賈元壽詞。

translations.literal: The stele inscription for Beimang Temple was composed by Vice Director of the Secretariat Jia Yuanshou.
translations.idiomatic: The Beimang Temple inscription was written by Vice Director of the Secretariat Jia Yuanshou.

sentences.zh: 孝文頻登北芒寺，親讀碑文，稱為佳作。

translations.literal: Xiaowen often climbed Beimang Temple, read the inscription himself, and praised it as excellent work.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen often visited Beimang Temple, read the inscription himself, and praised it as fine writing.

sentences.zh: 熙為州，因取人子女為奴婢，有容色者幸之為妾，有子女數十人，號為貪縱。

translations.literal: As governor, Xi took people's sons and daughters as slaves; those with beauty he favored as concubines, and he had several tens of children—hence he was called greedy and unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: In office he seized people's children as slaves; the comely he took as concubines and fathered dozens of children, earning a name for greed and license.

sentences.zh: 後授內都大官，太師如故。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Grand Official of the Inner Court, Grand Preceptor as before.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made Grand Official of the Inner Court, retaining Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 熙事魏母孝謹，如事所生。

translations.literal: Xi served Lady Wei with filial care, as if she were his birth mother.
translations.idiomatic: Xi tended Lady Wei with filial devotion, as to his own mother.

sentences.zh: 魏母卒，乃散發徒跣，水漿不入口三日。

translations.literal: When Lady Wei died, he loosed his hair and went barefoot, taking no food or drink for three days.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Wei died he unbound his hair and went barefoot, refusing food and drink for three days.

sentences.zh: 詔不聽服，熙表求依趙氏之孤。

translations.literal: An edict forbade mourning dress, but Xi memorialized asking to follow the precedent of the Zhao orphan.
translations.idiomatic: The throne forbade mourning garb, but Xi memorialized to follow the Zhao orphan precedent.

sentences.zh: 帝以熙情難奪，聽服齊衰期。

translations.literal: The emperor, seeing Xi's feeling could not be overcome, allowed him to wear the one-year mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, unable to sway him, let him observe one-year mourning.

sentences.zh: 後以例降，改封京兆郡公。

translations.literal: Later, by precedent his rank was reduced and his fief changed to Duke of Jingzhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Later, by precedent, his rank was lowered and his fief changed to Duke of Jingzhao Commandery.

sentences.zh: 帝納其女為後，曰：「《白武通》云：王所不臣，數有三焉。

translations.literal: The emperor took his daughter as empress and said, "The Baihu tong says: 'Those whom the king does not treat as subjects are three in number.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made his daughter empress and said, "The Baihu tong states: 'There are three whom the king does not treat as subjects.

sentences.zh: 妻之父母，抑言其一。

translations.literal: One's wife's parents—when speaking of them, one suppresses mention and names only one.
translations.idiomatic: In speaking of a wife's parents, custom allows naming only one of them.

sentences.zh: 此所謂供承宗廟，不欲奪私心。

translations.literal: This is what is called serving the ancestral temple and not wishing to indulge private feeling.
translations.idiomatic: That is the rule of honoring the ancestral temple without letting private affection override it.

sentences.zh: 然吾季著於《春秋》，無臣證於往牒，既許通體之一，用開至尊之敬。

translations.literal: Yet our younger sister appears in the Spring and Autumn Annals, and former documents offer no proof of subject status; since the unity of the whole person is permitted, supreme reverence may be opened.
translations.idiomatic: Yet our younger sister is recorded in the Spring and Autumn Annals, and no earlier text proves she was a subject; once the whole person is acknowledged, the highest reverence may follow.

sentences.zh: 比長秋配極，陰政既敷，未聞有司，陳奏斯式。

translations.literal: When Changqiu matched Heaven and feminine governance was already in place, one still did not hear the responsible offices memorialize this form.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the empress stood as Heaven's counterpart and the inner court held sway, no office had yet submitted this rite for approval.

sentences.zh: 可詔太師，輟臣從禮。」

translations.literal: It is fitting to order the Grand Preceptor to cease following the minister's rite."
translations.idiomatic: Let an edict tell the Grand Preceptor to stop observing the rites owed a minister."

sentences.zh: 又勒集書造儀付外。

translations.literal: An edict also ordered the Masters of Writing to draft the ceremony and issue it abroad.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also charged the Masters of Writing to draw up the ritual and publish it.

sentences.zh: 孝文前後納熙三女，二為後，一為左昭儀。

translations.literal: Before and after, Xiaowen took three of Xi's daughters; two became empresses and one became Left Lady of Bright Deportment.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen took three of Feng Xi's daughters in succession—two as empress, one as Left Lady of Bright Deportment.

sentences.zh: 由是馮氏寵貴益隆，賞賜累巨萬。

translations.literal: From this the Feng clan's favor and honors grew ever loftier, and rewards piled up to tens of millions.
translations.idiomatic: The Fengs rose still higher in favor and rank, with gifts running into the tens of millions.

sentences.zh: 帝每詔熙上書不臣，入朝不拜，熙上書如舊。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor ordered Xi to submit memorials without styling himself a subject or to enter court without bowing, Xi submitted memorials as before.
translations.idiomatic: Though the emperor repeatedly excused Xi from calling himself a subject in memorials or bowing at court, Xi kept to the old forms.

sentences.zh: 主生二子，誕、脩。

translations.literal: The principal wife bore two sons, Dan and Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: His chief wife bore two sons: Dan and Xiu.

sentences.zh: 誕字思正，脩字寶業，皆姿質妍麗。

translations.literal: Dan's style was Sizheng and Xiu's was Baoye; both were handsome in bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Dan, styled Sizheng, and Xiu, styled Baoye, were both striking in looks.

sentences.zh: 年才十餘，文明太后俱引入禁中，申以教誡。

translations.literal: While still little more than ten, Empress Dowager Wenming brought them both into the inner palace and personally instructed them.
translations.idiomatic: Before they were fifteen, Empress Dowager Wenming had both brought into the palace and tutored them herself.

sentences.zh: 然不能習讀經史，兄弟並無學術，徒整飾容儀，寬雅恭謹而已。

translations.literal: Yet they could not master the classics and histories; the brothers had no learning at all and only dressed their persons, remaining broad, elegant, and respectful.
translations.idiomatic: Neither could master the classics; the brothers had no real scholarship and only cultivated appearance—polite, easy, and correct.

sentences.zh: 誕與孝文同歲，幼侍書學，仍蒙親待，尚帝妹樂安長公主，拜駙馬都尉、侍中、征西大將軍、南平王。

translations.literal: Dan was the same age as Xiaowen; in youth he attended him in study and still received intimate favor, married the emperor's younger sister the Princess of Le'an, and was made Imperial Son-in-Law Commandant, Palace Attendant, General Who Conquers the West, and Prince of Nanping.
translations.idiomatic: Dan, Xiaowen's age-mate, had studied at his side as a boy and remained a favorite; he married the Princess of Le'an, became Imperial Son-in-Law Commandant, Palace Attendant, General Who Conquers the West, and Prince of Nanping.

sentences.zh: 脩侍中、鎮北大將軍、尚書、東平公。

translations.literal: Xiu was Palace Attendant, General Who Pacifies the North, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and Duke of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu served as Palace Attendant, General Who Pacifies the North, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and Duke of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 又除誕儀曹尚書，知殿中事。

translations.literal: Dan was also made Director of the Bureau of Appointments and put in charge of palace affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Dan was further named Director of the Bureau of Appointments and overseer of palace business.

sentences.zh: 及罷庶姓王，誕為侍中、都督中外諸軍事、中軍將軍、特進，改封長樂郡公。

translations.literal: When commoners' princely titles were abolished, Dan became Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs, General of the Central Army, Special Grand Master, and his fief was changed to Duke of Changle Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After non-imperial surnames were stripped of kingship, Dan became Palace Attendant, supreme commander, General of the Central Army, and Special Grand Master, enfeoffed as Duke of Changle Commandery.

sentences.zh: 誕拜官，孝文立於庭，遙受其拜，既訖還室。

translations.literal: When Dan received his appointment, Xiaowen stood in the hall and accepted his bow from afar; when it was done he returned to his chambers.
translations.idiomatic: At Dan's investiture Xiaowen stood in the courtyard and took his bow at a distance, then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 脩降為侯。

translations.literal: Xiu was reduced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu was demoted to marquis.

sentences.zh: 誕、脩雖並長宮禁，而性趣乖別。

translations.literal: Dan and Xiu had both grown up in the palace, yet their temperaments diverged.
translations.idiomatic: Though both were raised in the inner palace, Dan and Xiu were utterly unlike in character.

sentences.zh: 誕性淳篤，脩乃浮競。

translations.literal: Dan was sincere and steadfast by nature; Xiu was restless and competitive.
translations.idiomatic: Dan was plain and loyal; Xiu was flashy and ambitious.

sentences.zh: 誕亦未能誨督其過，然時言于太后。

translations.literal: Dan also could not instruct and correct his faults, yet from time to time he spoke of them to the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Dan could not discipline him, but he did report Xiu's conduct to the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 孝文嚴責之，至於楚捶。

translations.literal: Xiaowen sternly rebuked him, even to the point of beating him with the staff.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen rebuked him harshly and had him beaten.

sentences.zh: 由是陰懷毒恨，遂結左右有憾於誕者，求藥，欲因食害誕。

translations.literal: From this Xiu secretly nursed deadly hatred; he then joined with attendants who bore grudges against Dan, sought poison, and wished to kill Dan through his food.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu brooded on revenge and, with palace men who hated Dan, procured poison meant for Dan's meal.

sentences.zh: 事覺，帝自詰之，具得情狀。

translations.literal: When the affair was discovered, the emperor questioned him himself and learned the full circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: The plot came to light; the emperor interrogated him personally and learned every detail.

sentences.zh: 誕引過謝，乞全脩命。

translations.literal: Dan took the blame and begged pardon, asking that Xiu's life be spared.
translations.idiomatic: Dan accepted guilt on his own account and pleaded that Xiu be allowed to live.

sentences.zh: 帝以誕父老，又重其意，不致於法，撻之百餘，黜為平城百姓。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Dan was old in years and because he also valued Dan's intent, did not apply the law; he flogged him more than a hundred strokes and demoted him to commoner status in Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of Dan's age and his plea, the emperor spared the death penalty, gave Xiu a hundred-odd lashes, and banished him to common life at Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 脩妻，司空穆亮女也，求離婚，請免官。

translations.literal: Xiu's wife was the daughter of Minister of Works Mu Liang; she sought divorce and asked that her husband be dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu's wife, daughter of Mu Liang, Minister of Works, asked for divorce and for his dismissal.

sentences.zh: 帝引管、蔡事，皆不許。

translations.literal: The emperor cited the examples of Guan Zhong and Cai Shen, and in both matters he did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor invoked Guan Zhong and Duke Cai and refused both requests.

sentences.zh: 帝寵誕，仍作同輿而載，同案而食，同席坐臥。

translations.literal: The emperor favored Dan; he still rode in the same carriage, ate from the same tray, and sat or lay on the same mat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor doted on Dan—they shared carriage, table, and couch alike.

sentences.zh: 彭城王勰、北海王詳雖直禁中，然親近不及。

translations.literal: Prince Pengcheng Xie and Prince Beihai Xiang, though they attended within the forbidden quarters, were not so close.
translations.idiomatic: Princes Pengcheng and Beihai were in the inner precincts, yet none were as near to him as Dan.

sentences.zh: 十六年，以誕為司徒。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year Dan was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In year sixteen Dan was appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 帝既愛誕，除官日，親為制三讓表，並啟。

translations.literal: Because the emperor loved Dan, on the day of his appointment he personally drafted a threefold declination memorial and presented it with a memorial of request.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Dan took office the emperor, out of affection, wrote the threefold declination and the petition himself.

sentences.zh: 將拜，又為其章謝。

translations.literal: When the investiture was to take place, he again composed the letter of thanks on Dan's behalf.
translations.idiomatic: At the ceremony of appointment he again wrote Dan's letter of thanks.

sentences.zh: 尋加車騎大將軍、太子太師。

translations.literal: Soon he was further made General of Chariots and Cavalry and Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon added General of Chariots and Cavalry and Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十八年，帝謂其無師傅獎導風，誕深自誨責。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year the emperor said he lacked a tutor's guidance in fostering moral tone; Dan deeply reproached himself.
translations.idiomatic: In year eighteen the emperor said Dan had failed as a moral guide; Dan blamed himself bitterly.

sentences.zh: 從駕南伐，十九年，至鐘離。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign south; in the nineteenth year they reached Zhongli.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the southern campaign; in year nineteen the army reached Zhongli.

sentences.zh: 誕遇疾，不能侍從，帝日省問，醫藥備加。

translations.literal: Dan fell ill and could not attend; the emperor visited him daily and medicines were provided in full.
translations.idiomatic: Dan grew too ill to attend; the emperor inquired each day and saw that he had every remedy.

sentences.zh: 帝銳意臨江，乃命六軍發鐘離南轅，與誕泣訣。

translations.literal: The emperor was bent on crossing the river; he then ordered the six armies to march south from Zhongli and took tearful leave of Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Intent on the Yangzi crossing, he set the six armies moving south from Zhongli and parted from Dan in tears.

sentences.zh: 左右皆入，無不掩涕。

translations.literal: Those at hand all entered; none failed to cover their faces and weep.
translations.idiomatic: Every attendant who went in came out weeping.

sentences.zh: 時誕已惙然，強坐視帝，悲而淚不能下，言「夢太后來呼臣「。

translations.literal: By then Dan was already failing; he forced himself to sit and look at the emperor, grieved yet unable to shed tears, and said, "I dreamed the empress dowager calling me—
translations.idiomatic: Dan was near death; he sat up to gaze at the emperor, too stricken to cry, and murmured, "I dreamed the empress dowager summoning me—

sentences.zh: 帝嗚咽，執手而出，遂行。

translations.literal: The emperor sobbed, took his hand, and went out, then set off.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept, clasped his hand, left, and marched on.

sentences.zh: 是日，去鐘離五十里許，昏時，告誕薨問，帝哀不自勝。

translations.literal: That day, having gone perhaps fifty li from Zhongli, at dusk came word of Dan's death; the emperor's grief was beyond bearing.
translations.idiomatic: That same day, some fifty li from Zhongli, at dusk came news of Dan's death; the emperor was overcome.

sentences.zh: 時崔慧景、裴叔業軍在中淮，去所次不過百里，帝乃輕駕西還，從者數千人，夜至誕薨所。

translations.literal: At the time Cui Huijing and Pei Shuye's armies were on the central Huai, not a hundred li from where he halted; the emperor then returned west with a light escort of several thousand men and reached Dan's deathbed by night.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Huijing and Pei Shuye were encamped on the central Huai, less than a hundred li away; the emperor turned west with a few thousand riders and reached Dan before dawn.

sentences.zh: 拊屍哀慟，若喪至戚，達旦聲淚不絕。

translations.literal: He beat the corpse and wailed in anguish as if for his closest kin, and until dawn sound and tears did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: He embraced the body and mourned as for kin, weeping without pause until daylight.

sentences.zh: 從者亦迭舉音。

translations.literal: Those who followed also took turns raising their voices in lament.
translations.idiomatic: His attendants too broke into lament in turn.

sentences.zh: 帝以所服衣幍充襚，親自臨視，徹樂去膳，宣敕六軍，止臨江之駕。

translations.literal: The emperor used the clothes and headcloth he had worn to supply the funeral wrapping, personally oversaw the laying out, stopped music and removed delicacies from the table, and proclaimed to the six armies to halt the drive on the river.
translations.idiomatic: He gave his own garments for the shroud, oversaw the laying-out himself, banned music and rich food, and ordered the six armies to abandon the river campaign.

sentences.zh: 帝親北度，慟哭極哀。

translations.literal: The emperor crossed north in person and wept with utmost grief.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the river north himself and wept with desperate grief.

sentences.zh: 喪至洛陽，車駕猶在鐘離。

translations.literal: When the coffin reached Luoyang the imperial carriage was still at Zhongli.
translations.idiomatic: The bier reached Luoyang while the emperor remained at Zhongli.

sentences.zh: 詔留守賜賻物布帛五千匹、穀五千斛，以供葬事。

translations.literal: An edict to the capital garrison granted five thousand bolts of silk and cloth and five thousand hu of grain to supply the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: The capital garrison was ordered to send five thousand bolts of silk and cloth and five thousand hu of grain for the burial.

sentences.zh: 贈假黃鉞、使持節、大司馬，領司徒、侍中、都督，太師、駙馬、公如故。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the Acting Yellow Battle-Ax, credentials as envoy, and the post of Grand Marshal, retaining Minister of Works, Palace Attendant, area command, Grand Preceptor, Imperial Son-in-Law Commandant, and duke as before.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he received the Acting Yellow Battle-Ax, credentials as envoy, Grand Marshal, and kept Minister of Works, Palace Attendant, command authority, Grand Preceptor, Imperial Son-in-Law Commandant, and his ducal title.

sentences.zh: 加以殊禮，備錫九命，依晉大司馬、齊王攸故事。

translations.literal: Extraordinary rites were added and the Nine Bestowals were granted in full, following the precedents of the Jin Grand Marshal and Prince Xian of Qi, Sima You.
translations.idiomatic: Special honors and the full Nine Bestowals followed the precedents of Jin's Grand Marshal and Prince Xian of Qi, Sima You.

sentences.zh: 有司奏諡，詔曰：「案諡法，主善行德曰元，柔克有光曰懿。

translations.literal: The responsible offices submitted a posthumous title; the edict said: "According to the laws of posthumous naming, one who chiefly practices good conduct and virtue is called Yuan, and one who is gentle and overcomes yet shines is called Yi.
translations.idiomatic: When the offices proposed a posthumous name, the edict read: "By the rules of posthumous naming, he who chiefly embodies virtue is Yuan, and he who is gentle yet radiant is Yi.

sentences.zh: 昔貞惠兼美，受三諡之榮；

translations.literal: In former times steadfast grace combined with beauty and received the glory of three posthumous names;
translations.idiomatic: Of old, steadfast grace and beauty together won three posthumous epithets;

sentences.zh: 忠武雙徽，錫兩號之茂。

translations.literal: loyalty and martial prowess paired in emblems and were granted the splendor of two titles.
translations.idiomatic: loyalty and martial fame paired won two glorious names.

sentences.zh: 式准前訓，宜契具瞻。

translations.literal: Following the former instruction, the name should meet what all look up to.
translations.idiomatic: We follow those examples; the name should command universal regard.

sentences.zh: 既自少綢繆，知之惟朕，案行定名，諡曰元懿。」

translations.literal: From youth we were bound close, and none knew him as I; examining his conduct and fixing his name, the posthumous title is Yuan Yi.
translations.idiomatic: We were close from boyhood and I alone knew him truly; weighing his deeds, his posthumous title shall be Yuan Yi.

sentences.zh: 帝又親為作碑文及輓歌詞，皆窮美盡哀，事過其厚。

translations.literal: The emperor also personally composed the stele inscription and dirge lyrics, all exhausting beauty and grief, more lavish than was due.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor himself wrote the epitaph and dirges—every line strained for beauty and sorrow, beyond what custom required.

sentences.zh: 車駕還京，遂親至誕墓，停車而哭。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to the capital he went in person to Dan's tomb, halted the chariot, and wept.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to the capital he visited Dan's tomb in person, stopped his carriage, and wept.

sentences.zh: 使彭城王勰詔群官脫硃衣，服單衣介幘而哭司徒，貴者示以朋友，微者示如僚佐。

translations.literal: He sent Prince Pengcheng Xie to instruct the officials to remove their vermilion robes, wear plain single garments and simple caps, and mourn the Minister of Works; for the eminent he showed the grief of friends, for the humble that of subordinates.
