translations.idiomatic: Prince Pengcheng was sent to tell officials to shed vermilion robes, dress in plain clothes and simple caps, and mourn the Minister of Works—friends for the great, subordinates for the low.

sentences.zh: 公主貞厚有禮度，產二男。

translations.literal: The princess was chaste, generous, and observant of ritual; she bore two sons.
translations.idiomatic: The princess was steady, courteous, and bore two sons.

sentences.zh: 長子穆，字孝和，襲熙爵，避皇子愉封，改封扶風郡公。

translations.literal: The eldest son Mu, styled Xiaohe, inherited Xi's title; to avoid the enfeoffment of the imperial son Yu, the fief was changed to Duke of Fufeng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest, Mu, styled Xiaohe, inherited Xi's rank; when Prince Yu was enfeoffed, Mu's fief was changed to Duke of Fufeng Commandery.

sentences.zh: 尚孝文女順陽長公主，拜駙馬都尉，曆員外通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He married Xiaowen's daughter the Princess of Shunyang, was made Imperial Son-in-Law Commandant, and served in succession as Supernumerary Regular Attendant and Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He married the Princess of Shunyang, became Imperial Son-in-Law Commandant, and rose through supernumerary and regular attendant posts.

sentences.zh: 穆與叔輔興不和。

translations.literal: Mu was on bad terms with his uncle Fuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Mu quarreled with his uncle Fuxing.

sentences.zh: 輔興亡，贈相州刺史，祖載在庭，而穆方高車良馬，恭受職命，言宴滿堂，忻笑自若，為御史中尉、東平王匡所劾。

translations.literal: When Fuxing died and was posthumously made Governor of Xiangzhou, his grandfather's bier was already in the hall while Mu, in a fine carriage with good horses, respectfully received his appointment; he spoke at a full banquet and smiled with ease—for this he was impeached by the Censor-in-Chief, Prince Dongping Kuang.
translations.idiomatic: When Fuxing died, posthumously named Governor of Xiangzhou, the grandfather's coffin was in the hall while Mu, in splendid equipage, took up his commission, feasted, and laughed openly—Prince Dongping Kuang, as Censor-in-Chief, impeached him.

sentences.zh: 後位金紫光祿大夫，遇害河陰，贈司空、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he reached Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Tassel and was killed at Heyin; posthumously he was made Minister of Works and Governor of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later became Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Tassel, died at Heyin, and was posthumously Minister of Works and Governor of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 子冏，字景昭，襲爵昌黎王。

translations.literal: His son Jiong, styled Jingzhao, inherited the title Prince of Changli.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jiong, styled Jingzhao, inherited as Prince of Changli.

sentences.zh: 尋以庶姓罷王，仍襲扶風郡公。

translations.literal: Soon, because he was of common surname, kingship was abolished; he still inherited the title Duke of Fufeng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When non-imperial surnames lost princely rank he remained Duke of Fufeng Commandery.

sentences.zh: 子峭，字子漢，齊受禪，例降。

translations.literal: His son Qiao, styled Zihan, when Qi received the Mandate was reduced by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qiao, styled Zihan, was demoted under Qi by the usual rule.

sentences.zh: 穆弟顥，襲父誕長樂郡公。

translations.literal: Mu's younger brother Hao inherited his father Dan's title as Duke of Changle Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Mu's younger brother Hao inherited Dan's duchy of Changle Commandery.

sentences.zh: 脩弟聿，字寶興，廢後同產兄也。

translations.literal: Xiu's younger brother Yu, styled Baoxing, was the uterine brother of the deposed empress.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu's younger brother Yu, styled Baoxing, shared the womb with the deposed empress.

sentences.zh: 位黃門郎、信都伯。

translations.literal: He held the posts of Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and Baron of Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: He was Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and Baron of Xindu.

sentences.zh: 後坐妹廢，免為長樂百姓。

translations.literal: Later, because his sister was deposed, he was dismissed and made a commoner of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: After his sister's deposition he was stripped of office and reduced to a Changle commoner.

sentences.zh: 宣武時，卒于河南尹。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xuanwu he died in office as Governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuanwu he died while serving as Governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 聿同產弟風，幼養于宮，文明太后特加愛念。

translations.literal: Yu's uterine younger brother Feng was reared in the palace from childhood; Empress Dowager Wenming showed him special affection.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's full brother Feng was raised in the palace from infancy and was specially cherished by Empress Dowager Wenming.

sentences.zh: 數歲賜爵至北平王，拜太子中庶子，出入禁闥，寵侔二兄。

translations.literal: Before he was many years old he was enfeoffed up to Prince of Beiping and made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent; he went in and out of the forbidden gates and enjoyed favor equal to his two elder brothers.
translations.idiomatic: While still a child he was enfeoffed as high as Prince of Beiping and made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, passing freely through the inner gates with favor matching his brothers.

sentences.zh: 孝文親政後，恩寵稍衰，降爵為侯。

translations.literal: After Xiaowen took power in person, favor gradually waned and his title was lowered to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xiaowen ruled in his own right, Feng's grace faded and he was demoted to marquis.

sentences.zh: 幽後立，乃復敘用。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Empress was established he was again employed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Empress came to power he was restored to office.

sentences.zh: 後死，亦冗散。

translations.literal: After her death he too was idly dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: After her death he too was cast aside without post.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈青州刺史。

translations.literal: On his death he was posthumously made Governor of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously named Governor of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 崔光之兼黃門也，與聿俱直。

translations.literal: When Cui Guang served concurrently as Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, he and Yu were on duty together.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Guang held the Yellow Gate concurrently, he and Yu shared the watch.

sentences.zh: 光每謂之曰：「君家富貴大盛，終必衰敗。」

translations.literal: Guang often said to him, "Your house's wealth and glory are at their height; in the end it must decline and fall.
translations.idiomatic: Guang would tell him, "Your clan's wealth and power are at their peak—you must fall in the end.

sentences.zh: 聿云：「我家何負四海，乃咒我也！」

translations.literal: Yu said, "What has my house done against the realm, that you curse me so!"
translations.idiomatic: Yu replied, "What wrong have we done the empire, that you curse us?"

sentences.zh: 光云：「以古推之，不可不慎。」

translations.literal: Guang said, "Judging by antiquity, you cannot but be careful."
translations.idiomatic: Guang said, "History says you cannot be careless."

sentences.zh: 時熙為太保，誕司徒、太子太傅，脩侍中、尚書，聿黃門，廢後在位，禮愛未弛。

translations.literal: At the time Xi was Grand Preceptor, Dan was Minister of Works and Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, Xiu was Palace Attendant and Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Yu was Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, and the deposed empress still held position—ritual honor had not slackened.
translations.idiomatic: Then Xi was Grand Preceptor, Dan Minister of Works and Heir Apparent's tutor, Xiu Palace Attendant and Director of the Secretariat, Yu at the Yellow Gate, and the empress still on the throne—honor had not yet broken.

sentences.zh: 是後歲餘，脩以罪棄，熙、誕喪亡，後廢，聿退。

translations.literal: A little more than a year later Xiu was cast out for crime, Xi and Dan died, the empress was deposed, and Yu withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year Xiu was disgraced, Xi and Dan were dead, the empress deposed, and Yu dismissed.

sentences.zh: 時人以為盛必衰也。

translations.literal: Men of the time took it as proof that fullness must give way to decline.
translations.idiomatic: People then said it proved that the peak must fall.

sentences.zh: 李惠，中山人，思皇后之父也。

translations.literal: Li Hui was a man of Zhongshan and father of the Reflective Empress.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hui of Zhongshan was father of the Reflective Empress.

sentences.zh: 父蓋，少知名，歷位殿中都官二尚書、左將軍、南郡公。

translations.literal: His father Gai was known from youth, and held in succession the posts of Director of the Palace Offices, Second Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Left General, and Duke of Nan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gai won early renown and rose through Director of Palace Offices, Second Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Left General, and Duke of Nan.

sentences.zh: 初，太武妹武威長公主，故涼王沮渠牧犍之妻。

translations.literal: At first, Emperor Taiwu's younger sister the Princess of Wuwei, former wife of Juqu Mujian, king of Northern Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Emperor Taiwu's sister the Princess of Wuwei had been wife to Juqu Mujian of Northern Liang.

sentences.zh: 太武平涼州，頗以公主通密計之助，故寵遇差隆，詔蓋尚焉。

translations.literal: When Taiwu pacified Liangzhou he greatly favored her because the princess had secretly aided his plans; an edict ordered Gai to marry her.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiwu conquered Liangzhou he favored her for the princess's secret help in his designs and ordered Gai to marry her.

sentences.zh: 蓋妻與氏以是出。

translations.literal: Gai's wife Lady Yu came forth from this.
translations.idiomatic: From this union came Gai's wife, Lady Yu.

sentences.zh: 後蓋加侍中、駙馬都尉、殿中都官尚書、右僕射。

translations.literal: Later Gai was further made Palace Attendant, Imperial Son-in-Law Commandant, Director of the Palace Offices, and Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Gai was later made Palace Attendant, Imperial Son-in-Law Commandant, Director of Palace Offices, and Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 卒官，贈征南大將軍、定州刺史、中山王，諡曰莊。

translations.literal: He died in office and was posthumously made General Who Conquers the South, Governor of Dingzhou, Prince of Zhongshan, with the posthumous title Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office, posthumously General Who Conquers the South, Governor of Dingzhou, Prince of Zhongshan, titled Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 惠弱冠襲父爵，妻襄城王韓頹女，生二女，長即後也。

translations.literal: Hui at twenty inherited his father's title, married the daughter of Prince Xiangcheng Han Tui, and begot two daughters—the elder became the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Hui at twenty succeeded his father, married Prince Xiangcheng's daughter Han Tui, and had two daughters; the elder became empress.

sentences.zh: 惠歷位散騎常侍、侍中，征西大將軍、秦益二州刺史，進爵為王。

translations.literal: Hui held in succession the posts of Regular Attendant, Palace Attendant, General Who Conquers the West, and Governor of Qin and Yi provinces, and was advanced to princely rank.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Regular Attendant, Palace Attendant, General Who Conquers the West, and Governor of Qin and Yi, and was raised to prince.

sentences.zh: 轉雍州刺史、征南大將軍，加長安鎮大將。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Governor of Yongzhou and General Who Conquers the South, and was added Grand General Who Guards Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He became Governor of Yongzhou and General Who Conquers the South, with the added title Grand General Who Guards Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 惠長於思察。

translations.literal: Hui excelled in keen reflection.
translations.idiomatic: Hui had a gift for shrewd observation.

sentences.zh: 雍州査事，有燕爭巢，鬥已累日，惠令人掩獲，試命綱紀斷之，並辭。

translations.literal: In Yongzhou a case was under review: two swallows fought over a nest for many days; Hui had men seize them secretly, tried ordering the clerks to decide it, and all declined.
translations.idiomatic: At Yongzhou two swallows had fought over a nest for days; Hui had them captured quietly, asked his clerks to judge, and all refused.

sentences.zh: 惠乃使卒以弱竹彈兩燕，既而一去一留，惠笑謂吏屬曰：「此留者自計為巢功重，彼去者既經楚痛，理無固心。」

translations.literal: Hui then had soldiers flick the two swallows with thin bamboo; presently one left and one stayed. Hui laughed and told his clerks, "The one that stayed reckons its nest-building labor the heavier; the one that left, having already suffered pain, by reason should not hold firm—"
translations.idiomatic: Hui had soldiers tap both birds with a light bamboo switch; one flew off, one remained. He smiled at his staff: "The stayer counts its nest-work the greater stake; the leaver, already hurt, has no heart to stay—

sentences.zh: 群下伏其深察。

translations.literal: His subordinates were awed by his penetrating insight.
translations.idiomatic: His officers marveled at how keenly he had read the case.

sentences.zh: 人有負鹽負薪者，同釋重簷息樹陰。

translations.literal: Two men came along, one carrying salt on his back and one carrying firewood; they set down their heavy loads beneath the eaves and rested in the shade of a tree.
translations.idiomatic: A salt-porter and a woodcutter set down their burdens under the eaves and rested together in the shade of a tree.

sentences.zh: 二人將行，爭一羊皮，各言藉背之物。

translations.literal: When the two were about to leave, they quarreled over a single sheepskin, each claiming it was what he carried on his back.
translations.idiomatic: As they prepared to go, they fought over one sheepskin, each insisting it was his own.

sentences.zh: 惠遣爭者出，顧州綱紀曰：「此羊皮可拷知主乎？」

translations.literal: Hui sent the disputants out and, turning to the prefectural staff, asked, "Can beating this sheepskin reveal its owner?"
translations.idiomatic: Hui dismissed the quarrelers, then asked his staff, "Can we beat this hide and learn who owns it?

sentences.zh: 群下咸無答者。

translations.literal: None of those present could answer.
translations.idiomatic: No one below knew what to say.

sentences.zh: 惠令人置羊皮席上，以杖擊之，見少鹽屑，「得其實矣。」

translations.literal: Hui had the sheepskin laid on a mat and struck it with a staff; a little salt dust appeared. "The truth is out," he said."
translations.idiomatic: He had the hide spread on a mat and beaten with a rod until a few grains of salt showed. "There is our proof," he said.

sentences.zh: 使爭者視之，負薪者乃伏而就罪。

translations.literal: He made the disputants look; the woodcarrier then prostrated himself and confessed his crime.
translations.idiomatic: When he made them look, the woodcutter knelt and accepted punishment.

sentences.zh: 凡所察究，多如此類，由是吏人莫敢欺犯。

translations.literal: In general, whatever he investigated was of this sort; from then on clerks and officers did not dare to deceive or offend him.
translations.idiomatic: Most of his inquiries went this way, and afterward no clerk dared cheat him.

sentences.zh: 後為開府儀同三司、青州刺史，王如故。

translations.literal: Later he became Commissioner with the credentials of an envoy, equal in honor to the Three Excellencies, and Governor of Qingzhou, retaining his princely title.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Commissioner Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies and Governor of Qingzhou, while keeping his royal title.

sentences.zh: 曆政有美績。

translations.literal: In successive administrations he left fine achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Term after term he left a record of good governance.

sentences.zh: 惠素為文明太后所忌。

translations.literal: Hui had long been an object of Empress Dowager Wenming's resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wenming had long resented him.

sentences.zh: 誣惠將南叛，誅之。

translations.literal: She falsely charged that Hui was about to rebel in the south and had him executed.
translations.idiomatic: She accused him of plotting a southern rebellion and put him to death.

sentences.zh: 惠二弟初、樂與惠諸子同戮。

translations.literal: Hui's two younger brothers Chu and Yue were executed together with all of Hui's sons.
translations.idiomatic: His brothers Chu and Yue and all his sons were killed with him.

sentences.zh: 後妻梁氏亦死青州，盡沒其家財。

translations.literal: His later wife, the Lady Liang, also died in Qingzhou, and the family's entire property was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: His second wife, Lady Liang, died in Qingzhou as well, and the whole household estate was seized.

sentences.zh: 惠本無釁故，天下冤惜焉。

translations.literal: Hui had truly committed no offense; all under Heaven grieved at the injustice.
translations.idiomatic: He had done nothing to deserve it, and the realm mourned the wrong done him.

sentences.zh: 惠從弟鳳為定州刺史、安縣王長樂主簿。

translations.literal: Hui's cousin Feng served as Governor of Dingzhou and chief clerk to the Prince of An County, Prince Changle.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Feng was Governor of Dingzhou and chief clerk to Prince Changle of An County.

sentences.zh: 後長樂以罪賜死，時卜筮者河間邢瓚辭引鳳，雲長樂不軌，鳳為謀主，伏誅。

translations.literal: Later Prince Changle was ordered to die for his crimes; at the time the diviner Xing Zan of Hejian, in his testimony, implicated Feng, saying Changle had plotted treason and Feng was the chief plotter, and Feng was executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Changle was condemned to death, the diviner Xing Zan of Hejian named Feng as the ringleader of his treason, and Feng was executed.

sentences.zh: 唯鳳弟道念與鳳子及兄弟之子皆逃免，後遇赦乃出。

translations.literal: Only Feng's younger brother Daonian, Feng's son, and the sons of his brothers escaped; they came forth only after an amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Only Daonian, Feng's son, and their cousins escaped and emerged after a general pardon.

sentences.zh: 太和十二年，孝文將爵舅氏，詔訪存者。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Taihe, when Emperor Xiaowen was about to ennoble the maternal clan, an edict sought out survivors.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe year 12, as Emperor Xiaowen prepared to ennoble his mother's kin, he ordered a search for survivors.

sentences.zh: 而惠諸從以再離孥戮，難於應命。

translations.literal: But Hui's collateral kin, having twice suffered the slaughter of wives and children, found it hard to answer the summons.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's kinsmen, twice stripped of wives and children in mass executions, hesitated to come forward.

sentences.zh: 唯道念敢先詣闕，乃申後妹及鳳兄弟子女之存者。

translations.literal: Only Daonian dared go first to the palace and report which of the empress's younger sisters and of Feng's brothers, children, and grandchildren still lived.
translations.idiomatic: Only Daonian dared present himself at court and name the surviving younger sisters of the empress and the children of Feng's line.

sentences.zh: 於是賜鳳子屯爵柏人侯，安祖浮陽侯，興祖安喜侯，道念真定侯，從弟寄生高邑子，皆加將軍。

translations.literal: Thereupon Feng's son Tun was granted the rank of Marquis of Boren; Anzu, Marquis of Fuyang; Xingzu, Marquis of Anxi; Daonian, Marquis of Zhending; and the cousin Jisheng, Viscount of Gaoyi—all were also made generals.
translations.idiomatic: Feng's son Tun became Marquis of Boren; Anzu, Marquis of Fuyang; Xingzu, Marquis of Anxi; Daonian, Marquis of Zhending; and cousin Jisheng, Viscount of Gaoyi, each with a general's commission.

sentences.zh: 十五年，安祖昆弟四人，以外戚蒙見。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, the four brothers of the Anzu line, as maternal kin, were received in audience.
translations.idiomatic: In year 15, Anzu and his three brothers were summoned as consort kin.

sentences.zh: 詔謂曰：「卿之先世，內外有犯，得罪于時。

translations.literal: An edict told them, "Your forebears, within and without the family, committed offenses and were punished in their time.
translations.idiomatic: The throne told them, "Your ancestors, inside the clan and out, broke the law and paid for it in their day.

sentences.zh: 然官必用才，以親非興邦之選。

translations.literal: Yet office must employ talent; kinship is not what raises a state.
translations.idiomatic: Yet posts demand ability—blood ties are not how a state is built.

sentences.zh: 外氏之寵，超於末葉。

translations.literal: Favor to the maternal clan has exceeded what the late age should bear.
translations.idiomatic: Favor shown to consort families has outrun what these times can bear.

sentences.zh: 從今已後，自非奇才，不得復外戚謬班抽舉。

translations.literal: From this time forward, unless one is a rare talent, no maternal kinsman may again be rashly promoted out of rank.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth no maternal relative may be lifted out of turn unless he is truly exceptional.

sentences.zh: 既無殊能，今且可還。」

translations.literal: Since you have no special ability, for now you may withdraw."
translations.idiomatic: You have shown no special gift—go home for now.

sentences.zh: 後例降爵，宜祖等改侯為伯，並去軍號。

translations.literal: Later, by precedent their ranks were reduced: Yizu and the others were changed from marquises to earls, and all military titles were removed.
translations.idiomatic: Later their titles were lowered by precedent: Yizu and the rest became earls instead of marquises, and their general's commissions were stripped.

sentences.zh: 帝奉馮氏過厚，于李氏過薄，舅家了無敘用，朝野人士，所以竊議。

translations.literal: The emperor treated the Feng clan too generously and the Li clan too meagerly; the maternal Li house received no orderly employment, and court and countryside alike whispered about it.
translations.idiomatic: He favored the Fengs too richly and the Lis too thinly; Li kinsmen were given no proper posts, and gossip ran through court and country.

sentences.zh: 太常高閭，顯言於禁中。

translations.literal: The Minister of Ceremonies Gao Lü spoke plainly within the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Ceremonies Gao Lü spoke bluntly inside the palace.

sentences.zh: 及宣武寵隆外家，並居顯位。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu lavished favor on the maternal clan, they all held exalted posts.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowu the consort families rose to high office.

sentences.zh: 乃惟孝文舅氏，存已不沾恩澤。

translations.literal: Yet only Emperor Xiaowen's maternal kin, living or dead, received no grace.
translations.idiomatic: Only Emperor Xiaowen's mother's kin, whether alive or dead, had never tasted imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 景明末，特詔興祖為中山太守。

translations.literal: At the end of the Jingming era, a special edict made Xingzu Governor of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Jingming, Xingzu was specially appointed Governor of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 正始初，詔追崇惠為使持節、驃騎將軍、開府儀同三司、定州刺史、中山公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengshi, an edict posthumously honored Hui as Commissioner with the credentials of an envoy, General of Agile Cavalry, Commissioner Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, Governor of Dingzhou, and Duke of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Zhengshi, Hui was posthumously made Commissioner with Full Powers, General of Agile Cavalry, Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, Governor of Dingzhou, and Duke of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 太常考行，上言：案諡法，武而不遂曰壯，諡曰壯公。

translations.literal: The Minister of Ceremonies examined his conduct and memorialized: According to the rules of posthumous names, "martial yet unfulfilled" is Zhuang; his posthumous title is Duke Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Ceremonies reviewed his life and reported: by the naming code, "bold but uncompleted" yields Zhuang—thus Duke Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 興祖自中山遷燕州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: Xingzu moved from Zhongshan to Governor of Yanzhou and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzu was transferred from Zhongshan to Yanzhou and died there.

sentences.zh: 以兄安祖子侃晞為後，襲先封南郡王。

translations.literal: His elder brother Anzu's son Kan Xi was made heir and inherited the former enfeoffment as Prince of Nan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Anzu's son Kan Xi was adopted as heir and succeeded to the old title, Prince of Nan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 後以庶姓罷王，改為博陵郡公。

translations.literal: Later, because they were of common surname, the princely title was revoked and he was made Duke of Boling Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Later the royal title was withdrawn as a non-imperial surname, and he became Duke of Boling Commandery.

sentences.zh: 侃晞為莊帝所親幸，拜散騎常侍、嘗食典禦。

translations.literal: Kan Xi was a favorite of Emperor Zhuang and was appointed Attendant Cavalier and Master of the Imperial Tasters.
translations.idiomatic: Kan Xi won Emperor Zhuang's trust and was made Attendant Cavalier and Master of the Imperial Tasters.

sentences.zh: 帝之圖爾硃榮，侃晞與魯安等持刃於禁內殺榮。

translations.literal: When the emperor plotted against Erzhu Rong, Kan Xi and Lu An and others, blades in hand, killed Rong within the forbidden quarters.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor moved against Erzhu Rong, Kan Xi and Lu An killed him inside the palace with drawn swords.

sentences.zh: 及莊帝蒙塵，侃晞奔梁。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang fell into hardship, Kan Xi fled to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang was overthrown, Kan Xi escaped to Liang.

sentences.zh: 高肇，字首文，文昭皇太后之兄也。

translations.literal: Gao Zhao, style Shouwen, was elder brother to Empress Dowager Wenming.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhao, courtesy name Shouwen, was the elder brother of Empress Dowager Wenming.

sentences.zh: 自雲本勃海蓚人。

translations.literal: From Yun onward the clan was originally from Mao in Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: From Gao Yun's generation the family was native to Mao in Bohai.

sentences.zh: 五世祖顧，晉永嘉中，避亂入高麗。

translations.literal: The fifth-generation ancestor Gu, in the Yongjia era of Jin, fled turmoil and entered Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: His fifth-generation ancestor Gu fled the Yongjia disorders and took refuge in Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 父颺，字法脩。

translations.literal: His father Yang, style Faxiu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yang, courtesy name Faxiu.

sentences.zh: 孝文初，與弟乘信及其鄉人韓內、冀富等入魏，拜厲威將軍、河間子；

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowen's reign, together with his younger brother Chengxin and fellow townsmen Han Nei, Ji Fu, and others, he entered Wei and was appointed General of Stern Might and Viscount of Hejian;
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaowen's reign he entered Wei with his brother Chengxin and townsfolk Han Nei and Ji Fu; he was made General of Stern Might and Viscount of Hejian;

sentences.zh: 乘信明威將軍，俱待以客禮。

translations.literal: Chengxin was made General of Bright Might; both were treated with the courtesy due guests.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxin became General of Bright Might; both were received as honored guests.

sentences.zh: 遂納颺女，是為文昭皇后，生宣武。

translations.literal: The emperor then took Yang's daughter as consort—she became Empress Wenming and bore Emperor Xiaowu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor married Yang's daughter, who became Empress Wenming and mothered Emperor Xiaowu.

sentences.zh: 颺卒，景明初，宣武追思舅氏，征肇兄弟等。

translations.literal: When Yang died, at the beginning of the Jingming era Emperor Xiaowu, recalling his mother's kin, summoned Zhao and his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang's death, at the start of Jingming Emperor Xiaowu summoned Zhao and his brothers to court.

sentences.zh: 錄尚書事、北海王詳等奏，颺宜贈左光祿大夫，賜爵勃海公，諡曰敬。

translations.literal: The Recorder of the Affairs of the Master of Writing, the Prince of Beihai Xiang, and others memorialized that Yang should be posthumously made Left Grand Master of the Palace and enfeoffed as Duke of Bohai, with the posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Beihai Xiang and other recorders proposed posthumous honors for Yang: Left Grand Master of the Palace, Duke of Bohai, posthumous name Jing.

sentences.zh: 其妻蓋氏，宜追封清河郡君。

translations.literal: His wife, the Lady Gai, should be posthumously enfeoffed as Lady of Qinghe Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Gai should be named Lady of Qinghe Commandery.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict assented.

sentences.zh: 又詔颺嫡孫猛襲勃海公爵，封肇平原郡公，肇弟顯澄城郡公，三人同日受封。

translations.literal: Another edict made Yang's eldest grandson by the principal wife, Meng, inherit the ducal title of Bohai; Zhao was enfeoffed as Duke of Pingyuan Commandery and his younger brother Xian as Duke of Chengcheng Commandery—the three received their fiefs on the same day.
translations.idiomatic: Meng, Yang's legitimate grandson, inherited Bohai; Zhao became Duke of Pingyuan and Xian Duke of Chengcheng—all three enfeoffed the same day.

sentences.zh: 始宣武未與舅氏相接，將拜爵，乃賜衣幘，引見肇、顯于華林都亭。

translations.literal: At first Emperor Xiaowu had not yet met his maternal kin; when he was about to grant titles, he bestowed robes and caps and received Zhao and Xian at the Dueting in the Hualin Park.
translations.idiomatic: Before meeting his mother's kin, he gave them robes and caps and received Zhao and Xian at the Hualin Park pavilion.

sentences.zh: 皆甚惶懼，舉動失儀，數日之間，富貴赫奕。

translations.literal: Both were deeply fearful; their movements lost propriety, yet within a few days wealth and splendor blazed about them.
translations.idiomatic: They were terrified and awkward in ceremony, yet within days they blazed with sudden fortune.

sentences.zh: 是年，咸陽王禧誅，財物珍寶、奴婢、田宅多入高氏。

translations.literal: That year Prince Xianyang of Xian was executed; treasures, valuables, slaves, fields, and houses mostly passed into the Gao clan.
translations.idiomatic: That year Prince Xianyang Xi was put to death, and most of his wealth, slaves, and estates flowed to the Gaos.

sentences.zh: 未幾，肇為尚書右僕射、冀州大中正，尚宣武姑高平公主，遷尚書令。

translations.literal: Before long Zhao became Vice Director of the Master of Writing and Grand Rectifier of Ji Province; he married Emperor Xiaowu's paternal aunt, the Princess of Gaoping, and was promoted to Director of the Master of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhao was Vice Director of the Master of Writing and Ji Province's Grand Rectifier; he married the Princess of Gaoping and rose to Director of the Master of Writing.

sentences.zh: 肇出自夷土，時望輕之。

translations.literal: Zhao came from barbarian soil, and contemporary esteem for him was slight.
translations.idiomatic: Born beyond the frontier, he was lightly regarded at first.

sentences.zh: 及在位居要，留心百揆，孜孜無倦，世咸謂之為能。

translations.literal: Once he held a key post, he attended to the hundred offices with tireless care; the age broadly called him capable.
translations.idiomatic: In high office he labored over every branch of government without rest, and many called him able.

sentences.zh: 宣武初，六輔專政，後以咸陽王禧無事構逆，由是委肇。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign the six regents monopolized government; later, because Prince Xianyang Xi had plotted treason without cause, power was entrusted to Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Early on the six regents ruled; after Prince Xianyang's baseless treason, the emperor leaned on Zhao.

sentences.zh: 肇既無親族，頗結朋黨，附之者旬月超升，背之者陷以大罪。

translations.literal: Zhao had no kin of his own and therefore cultivated factions; those who attached to him were promoted within a month, while those who turned away were trapped in grave crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Lacking close kin, he built factions—followers vaulted upward in a month, opponents were buried in capital charges.

sentences.zh: 以北海王詳位居其上，構殺之。

translations.literal: Because the Prince of Beihai Xiang stood above him in rank, he framed and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: He destroyed Prince of Beihai Xiang, who outranked him.

sentences.zh: 又說宣武防衛諸王，殆同囚禁。

translations.literal: He also urged Emperor Xiaowu to guard the imperial princes so strictly that they were nearly prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: He persuaded the emperor to cage the princes under guard, nearly as captives.

sentences.zh: 時順皇后暴崩，世議言肇為之。

translations.literal: At that time the empress consort died suddenly; public talk said Zhao had done it.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress consort died abruptly, rumor blamed Zhao.

sentences.zh: 皇子昌薨，僉謂王顯失於醫療，承肇意旨。

translations.literal: When the prince Chang died, all agreed that Wang Xian had failed in medical care at Zhao's instigation.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Chang died, many said the physician Wang Xian had erred on Zhao's orders.

sentences.zh: 及京兆王愉出為冀州刺史，畏肇恣擅，遂至不軌。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Jingzhao Yu went out as Governor of Ji Province, he feared Zhao's arbitrary power and came to the brink of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jingzhao Yu, sent to Ji Province, feared Zhao's license and nearly rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 肇又譖殺彭城王勰。

translations.literal: Zhao also slandered and killed the Prince of Pengcheng Xie.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao also brought about the death of Prince of Pengcheng Xie.

sentences.zh: 由是朝野側目，咸畏惡之。

translations.literal: Because of this, court and countryside watched him sidelong; all feared and hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Court and country watched him with narrowed eyes and shared a common dread.

sentences.zh: 因此專權，與奪任己。

translations.literal: Thus he monopolized power and disposed of offices as he pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He seized power and gave or took office at will.

sentences.zh: 又嘗與清河王懌於雲門外廡下，忽忿諍，大至紛紜。

translations.literal: He also once quarreled violently with the Prince of Qinghe Yi beneath the colonnade outside the Cloud Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Once he erupted into a shouting brawl with Prince of Qinghe Yi under the Cloud Gate colonnade.

sentences.zh: 太尉、高陽王雍和止之。

translations.literal: The Grand Marshal, the Prince of Gaoyang Yong, reconciled them.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Prince of Gaoyang Yong forced peace between them.

sentences.zh: 高後既立，逾見寵信。

translations.literal: After the empress dowager was established, he was favored still more.
translations.idiomatic: Once the empress dowager reigned, his favor deepened.

sentences.zh: 肇既當衡軸，每事任己，本無學識，動違禮度。

translations.literal: Zhao, holding the axis of power, decided every affair by his own will; he had no learning and constantly violated ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: At the hub of government he ruled by whim; unlearned, he trampled ritual at every turn.

sentences.zh: 好改先朝舊制，減削封秩，抑黜勳人，由是怨聲盈路矣。

translations.literal: He loved to alter former dynasties' old institutions, cut ranks and fiefs, and suppress meritorious men; because of this, complaint filled the roads.
translations.idiomatic: He rewrote old institutions, pared fiefs, and humbled men of merit until resentment clogged the highways.

sentences.zh: 延昌初，遷司徒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yanxi era he was transferred to Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In early Yanxi he was made Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 雖貴登臺鼎，猶以去要怏怏，眾咸嗤笑之。

translations.literal: Though ennobled to the tripods of state, he was still displeased at losing the key post; the multitude all laughed at him.
translations.idiomatic: Though raised to the highest ministerial rank, he sulked at losing real power, and everyone mocked him.

sentences.zh: 父兄封贈雖久，竟不改瘞。

translations.literal: His father and elder brother had long received posthumous enfeoffment, yet he never moved their burial place.
translations.idiomatic: His father and brother had been ennobled posthumously, yet he left their graves unrestored.

sentences.zh: 三年，乃詔令還葬。

translations.literal: In the third year an edict at last ordered their remains returned for burial.
translations.idiomatic: Only in the third year did an edict command their reburial.

sentences.zh: 肇不自臨赴，唯遣其兄子猛改服詣代，遷葬於鄉。

translations.literal: Zhao did not go in person; he sent only his elder brother's son Meng, in mourning dress, to Dai to transfer the coffins for burial in their home district.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao stayed away and sent his nephew Meng in mourning garb to Dai to bring the coffins home.

sentences.zh: 時人以肇無識，哂而不責也。

translations.literal: People of the time, deeming Zhao ignorant, sneered yet did not blame him.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries, judging him witless, laughed but did not reproach him.

sentences.zh: 及大舉征蜀，以肇為大將軍、都督諸軍，為之節度。

translations.literal: When a great campaign was launched against Shu, Zhao was made Grand General and Commander of All Armies to regulate it.
translations.idiomatic: When the empire marched on Shu, Zhao was named Grand General and supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 與都督甄琛等二十餘人，俱面辭宣武於東堂，親奉規略。

translations.literal: Together with the commander Zhen Chen and more than twenty others, they all took leave of Emperor Xiaowu face to face in the Eastern Hall and personally received strategy.
translations.idiomatic: He and Commander Zhen Chen and twenty others took leave in the Eastern Hall and received the campaign plan from the emperor himself.

sentences.zh: 是日，肇所乘駿馬，停於神獸門外，無故驚倒，轉臥渠中，鞍具瓦解，眾咸怪異。

translations.literal: That day the fine horse Zhao rode halted outside the Divine Beast Gate, suddenly startled and thrown down; it rolled into a ditch, its saddle shattered—everyone found it strange.
translations.idiomatic: That day his stallion fell without cause outside the Divine Beast Gate, tumbling into a ditch with its tack broken—a omen everyone noted.

sentences.zh: 肇出，惡焉。

translations.literal: When Zhao went out, he took it as ill-omened.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao left troubled by the sign.

sentences.zh: 四年，宣武崩，赦，罷征軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Emperor Xiaowu died; an amnesty was proclaimed and the expeditionary army disbanded.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Emperor Xiaowu died; amnesty followed and the army was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 明帝與肇及征南將軍元遙等書，稱諱言以告凶問。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming wrote to Zhao and the Campaign General of the South Yuan Yao and others, using the tabooed name to announce the bereavement.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming wrote Zhao and Campaign General of the South Yuan Yao, naming the death with the imperial taboo.

sentences.zh: 肇承變，非唯仰慕，亦憂身禍，朝夕悲泣，至於羸悴。

translations.literal: When Zhao received the change, he was not only full of grief and longing but also fearful of disaster to himself; he wept morning and night until he wasted away.
translations.idiomatic: The news brought him grief and terror alike; he wept day and night until he withered.

sentences.zh: 將至，宿瀍澗驛亭，家人夜迎省之，皆不相視。

translations.literal: As he was about to arrive, he lodged at the Luanjian post station; his family came at night to visit, yet none would look at one another.
translations.idiomatic: Near the capital he stopped at Luanjian; his kin met him by night but none could meet the other's eyes.

sentences.zh: 直至闕下，縗服號哭，升太極殿，盡哀。

translations.literal: He went straight to the palace gate in hemp mourning, wailing as he ascended the Hall of Supreme Ultimate and exhausted his grief.
translations.idiomatic: He entered in coarse mourning, crying his way up the Hall of Supreme Ultimate until grief was spent.

sentences.zh: 太尉高陽王先居西柏堂，專決庶事，與領軍於忠，密欲除之。

translations.literal: The Grand Marshal Prince of Gaoyang had first occupied the Western Cypress Hall and decided common affairs alone; he and the Camp Commander Yu Zhong secretly wished to remove Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Prince of Gaoyang Yong, ruling from the Western Cypress Hall, conspired with Camp Commander Yu Zhong to kill him.

sentences.zh: 潛備壯士直寢邢豹、伊盆生等十餘人於舍人省下。

translations.literal: They secretly stationed more than ten stout warriors—Zhi Bao of the Direct Attendants' Quarters, Yi Pensheng, and others—in the Secretariat below.
translations.idiomatic: They hid a dozen strongmen—Zhi Bao, Yi Pensheng, and others—below the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 肇哭梓宮訖，於百官前引入西廓，清河王懌、任城王澄及諸王等皆竊言目之。

translations.literal: When Zhao had finished wailing before the coffin, he was led before the officials into the western corridor; the Prince of Qinghe Yi, the Prince of Rencheng Cheng, and the other princes all whispered and watched him with their eyes.
translations.idiomatic: After the coffin rites they drew him into the west corridor before the court; princes exchanged glances and murmured.

sentences.zh: 肇入省，壯士扼而拉殺之，下詔暴其罪惡，稱為自盡。

translations.literal: When Zhao entered the office, the warriors seized and strangled him; an edict exposed his crimes and called it suicide.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the office the bravoes throttled him; an edict listed his crimes and called it self-slaughter.

sentences.zh: 自餘親黨，悉無追問。

translations.literal: The rest of his kin were not pursued.
translations.idiomatic: His other relatives went unprosecuted.

sentences.zh: 削除職爵，葬以士禮。

translations.literal: His offices and titles were struck; he was buried with the rites due a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Stripped of rank, he was buried as a commoner.

sentences.zh: 逮昏，乃於廁門出其屍歸家。

translations.literal: Only at dusk was his corpse brought out through the privy gate and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk his body was shoved out the privy gate and carried home.

sentences.zh: 初肇西征，行至函谷，車軸中折，從者皆以為不獲吉還也。

translations.literal: When Zhao first marched west, he reached Hangu Pass; the axle of his carriage broke in two, and his attendants all took it as a sign he would not return in fortune.
translations.idiomatic: On his western campaign, at Hangu Pass his carriage axle snapped, and followers read it as a vow he would not come back whole.

sentences.zh: 靈太后臨朝，令特贈營州刺史。

translations.literal: When the Empress Dowager Ling held court, she specially posthumously made him Governor of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling later posthumously restored him as Governor of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 永熙二年，孝武帝贈使持節、侍中、中外諸軍事、太師、大丞相、太尉公、錄尚書事、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi, Emperor Xiaowu of the Northern Wei posthumously made him Commissioner with the credentials of an envoy, Palace Attendant, Commander of All Military Affairs Within and Without, Grand Preceptor, Grand Chancellor, Grand Marshal, Duke, Recorder of the Affairs of the Master of Writing, and Governor of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi year 2 Emperor Xiaowu posthumously heaped on him every grand title—Commissioner with Full Powers, Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief, Grand Preceptor, Grand Chancellor, Grand Marshal, Duke, Recorder of the Master of Writing, and Governor of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 肇子植，自中書侍郎為濟州刺史，率州軍討破元愉別將有功，當蒙封賞。

translations.literal: Zhao's son Zhi, from Secretariat Vice Director became Governor of Jizhou, led the provincial army to defeat a deputy general of Yuan Yu with merit, and ought to receive enfeoffment and reward.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi, son of Zhao, rose from Secretariat Vice Director to Governor of Jizhou; he led provincial troops to rout a lieutenant of Yuan Yu and earned rewards due him.

sentences.zh: 不受。

translations.literal: He did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He refused them.

sentences.zh: 云：「家荷重恩，為國致效，是其常節，何足以膺進陟之報？」

translations.literal: He said: "My family bears heavy favor; to render service to the state is our constant duty—how could that merit promotion and reward?
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Our house owes a great debt of grace; serving the state is only our proper duty—what claim have we to advancement and reward?

sentences.zh: 懇惻發于至誠。

translations.literal: His earnestness sprang from utmost sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: His plea came from the depths of sincerity.

sentences.zh: 曆青、相、朔、恆四州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: He served in succession as Governor of Qing, Xiang, Shuo, and Heng provinces, then died.
translations.idiomatic: He held Qing, Xiang, Shuo, and Heng in turn, then died.

sentences.zh: 植頻蒞五州，皆清能著稱，當時號為良刺史。

translations.literal: Zhi repeatedly governed five provinces, all winning renown for probity and ability; of his time he was called a good governor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi governed five provinces in all, each time earning praise for clean competence; men of the day called him a model governor.

sentences.zh: 贈安北將軍、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously made General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On his death he was made General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 肇長兄琨，早卒，襲颺封勃海郡公，贈都督五州諸軍事、鎮東大將軍、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: Zhao's elder brother Kun died early, inherited Feng's fief as Duke of Bohai, and was posthumously made Supervisor of Military Affairs for Five Provinces, General Who Pacifies the East, and Governor of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Kun, Zhao's elder brother, died young; he inherited Feng's Bohai dukedom and was posthumously named supervisor of five provinces' military affairs, General Who Pacifies the East, and Governor of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 詔其子猛嗣。

translations.literal: An edict ordered his son Meng to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict had his son Meng succeed.

sentences.zh: 猛字豹兒，尚長樂公主，即宣武同母妹也。

translations.literal: Meng, courtesy name Bao'er, married Princess Changle—Emperor Xuanwu's younger half-sister by the same mother.
translations.idiomatic: Meng, styled Bao'er, married Princess Changle, Xuanwu's uterine younger sister.

sentences.zh: 拜駙馬都尉，歷位中書令，出為雍州刺史，有能名。

translations.literal: He was appointed Commandant of the Horse Guards, rose to Secretariat Director, went out as Governor of Yongzhou, and won a name for ability.
translations.idiomatic: Made Commandant of the Horse Guards, he rose to Secretariat Director, then served as Governor of Yongzhou with a reputation for competence.

sentences.zh: 入為殿中尚書，卒。

translations.literal: He entered court as Director of the Palace Bureau and died.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as Director of the Palace Bureau, he died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈司空、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously made Minister of Works and Governor of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Minister of Works and Governor of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝時，復贈太師、大丞相、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xiaowu he was again posthumously made Grand Preceptor, Grand Chancellor, and Supervisor of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu later added Grand Preceptor, Grand Chancellor, and Supervisor of the Masters of Writing to his posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 公主無子，猛先在外有男，不敢令主知，臨終方言之，年歲三十矣。

translations.literal: The princess had no son; Meng had earlier had a son outside but dared not let the princess know; only at his death did he speak of it—the boy was thirty years old.
translations.idiomatic: The princess bore no children. Meng had fathered a son in secret and dared not tell her; only on his deathbed did he reveal him—a man of thirty.

sentences.zh: 乃召為喪主。

translations.literal: He was then summoned to be chief mourner.
translations.idiomatic: The son was summoned to head the funeral.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，無後。

translations.literal: Soon he too died, leaving no heir.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died as well, and the line ended.

sentences.zh: 琨弟偃，字仲遊。

translations.literal: Kun's younger brother Yan, courtesy name Zhongyou.
translations.idiomatic: Kun's younger brother Yan, styled Zhongyou.

sentences.zh: 太和十年，卒。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Taihe he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth year of Taihe.

sentences.zh: 正始中，贈安東將軍、都督、青州刺史，諡曰莊侯。

translations.literal: In the Zhengshi era he was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the East, Supervisor, and Governor of Qingzhou, with the posthumous title Marquis Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengshi he was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the East, supervisor, and Governor of Qingzhou, titled Marquis Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 景明四年，宣武納其女為貴嬪，及于順皇后崩，永平元年，立為皇后。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jingming Emperor Xuanwu took his daughter as Noble Consort; when Empress Shun died, in the first year of Yongping she was installed as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingming 4 Xuanwu took Yan's daughter as Noble Consort; after Empress Shun's death, Yongping 1 saw her raised to empress.

sentences.zh: 二年，八坐奏封後母王氏為武邑郡君。

translations.literal: In the second year the Eight Dignitaries memorialized to enfeoff the empress's mother Lady Wang as Lady of Wuyi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year the Eight Dignitaries asked that the empress's mother, Lady Wang, be made Lady of Wuyi Commandery.

sentences.zh: 偃弟壽，早卒。

translations.literal: Yan's younger brother Shou died early.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's younger brother Shou also died young.

sentences.zh: 壽弟即肇也。

translations.literal: Shou's younger brother was none other than Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Shou's younger brother was Zhao himself.

sentences.zh: 肇弟顯，侍中、高麗國大中正，早卒。

translations.literal: Zhao's younger brother Xian, Palace Attendant and Grand Umpire of Goguryeo, died early.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's younger brother Xian, Palace Attendant and grand umpire for Goguryeo, likewise died young.

sentences.zh: 胡國珍，字世玉，安定臨涇人也。

translations.literal: Hu Guozhen, courtesy name Shiyu, was a man of Linting in Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Guozhen, styled Shiyu, came from Linting in Anding commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖略，姚興勃海公姚逵平北府諮議參軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Lüe was Consultative Aide in the Pacify-the-North Staff of Yao Xing's Bohai Duke Yao Kui.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Lüe had served Yao Kui, Bohai duke under Yao Xing, as consultative aide on the Pacify-the-North staff.

sentences.zh: 父深，赫連屈丐給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: His father Shen was Attendant at the Yellow Gates under Helian Bobo.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shen was an Attendant at the Yellow Gates under Helian Bobo.

sentences.zh: 太武克統萬，深以降款之功，賜爵武始侯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taiwu took Tongwan, Shen for merits of surrender was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wushi.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taiwu captured Tongwan, Shen's timely surrender won him the marquisate of Wushi.

sentences.zh: 後拜河州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Governor of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Governor of Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 國珍少好學，雅尚清儉。

translations.literal: Guozhen in youth loved learning and admired frugality.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Guozhen loved learning and prized austerity.

sentences.zh: 太和十五年襲爵，例降為伯。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Taihe he inherited the title, which by precedent was lowered to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 15 he inherited the title, reduced by precedent from duke to marquis.

sentences.zh: 女以選入掖庭，生明帝，即靈太后也。

translations.literal: His daughter was selected into the rear palace and bore Emperor Ming—that is, Empress Dowager Ling.
translations.idiomatic: His daughter entered the inner palace and bore Emperor Ming—none other than Empress Dowager Ling.

sentences.zh: 孝明帝踐祚，以國珍為光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended, Guozhen was made Grand Counselor of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: At Ming's accession Guozhen was made Grand Counselor of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 靈太后臨朝，加侍中，封安定郡公。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling held court, he was made Palace Attendant and enfeoffed Duke of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Once the empress dowager ruled, he became Palace Attendant and Duke of Anding.

sentences.zh: 追崇國珍妻皇甫氏為京兆郡君，置守塚十戶。

translations.literal: Guozhen's wife Lady Huangfu was posthumously enfeoffed Lady of Jingzhao Commandery, with ten households appointed tomb guardians.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Huangfu, Guozhen's wife, was posthumously made Lady of Jingzhao Commandery; ten households were set to guard the tomb.

sentences.zh: 尚書令、任城王澄奏，安定公宜出入禁中，參諮大務。

translations.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing, Prince of Rencheng Cheng memorialized that the Duke of Anding should enter the forbidden precinct and take part in great affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Director Cheng of Rencheng urged that the Duke of Anding enter the inner palace and counsel on weighty matters.

sentences.zh: 詔屈公入決萬機。

translations.literal: An edict had the duke enter to decide the myriad affairs.
translations.idiomatic: An edict brought the duke in to decide state business.

sentences.zh: 尋進位中書監、儀同三司，侍中如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to Supervisor of the Secretariat and Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, retaining Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Supervisor of the Secretariat and Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, still Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 賜絹，歲八百疋，妻梁四百匹，男女姊妹各有差。

translations.literal: He was granted eight hundred bolts of silk yearly; his wife Liang four hundred; male and female siblings each had their allotment.
translations.idiomatic: He received eight hundred bolts of silk a year, his wife Liang four hundred, and each sibling a graded share.

sentences.zh: 國珍與太師高陽王雍、太傅清河王懌、太保廣平王懷入居門下，同厘庶政。

translations.literal: Guozhen with Grand Preceptor, Prince of Gaoyang Yong, Grand Tutor, Prince of Qinghe Yi, and Grand Guardian, Prince of Guangping Huai entered the Gate Below to share in ordinary government together.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen joined Grand Preceptor Yong of Gaoyang, Grand Tutor Yi of Qinghe, and Grand Guardian Huai of Guangping below the gate to govern together.

sentences.zh: 詔依漢車千秋、晉安平王故事，給步挽一乘，自掖門至於宣光殿，得以出入，並備几杖。

translations.literal: An edict, following the precedents of Han's Che Qianqiu and Jin's Prince of Anping, granted one palanquin with bearers from the Rear Gate to Xuanguang Hall for coming and going, with tables and staffs provided.
translations.idiomatic: By edict, on the model of Che Qianqiu of Han and the Prince of Anping of Jin, he received a palanquin from the Rear Gate to Xuanguang Hall and was furnished with table and staff.

sentences.zh: 後與侍中崔光，俱授帝經，侍直禁中。

translations.literal: Later he and Palace Attendant Cui Guang together instructed the emperor in the classics and attended in the forbidden precinct.
translations.idiomatic: Later he and Palace Attendant Cui Guang tutored the emperor and kept watch in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 國珍上表陳刑政之宜，詔皆施行。

translations.literal: Guozhen memorialized on what was fitting in punishments and government; the edicts all put his proposals into effect.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen submitted views on law and administration; the throne enacted them all.

sentences.zh: 延和初，加國珍使持節、都督、雍州刺史，驃騎大將軍開府。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yanhe he was further made Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor, and Governor of Yongzhou, with an established staff as General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yanhe he was given the staff, made supervisor and Governor of Yongzhou, and opened a staff as General of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 靈太后以國珍年老，不欲令其在外，且欲示以方面之榮，竟不行。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling, because Guozhen was old, did not wish him to go outside, yet wished to show him the glory of a frontier post—and in the end he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager, deeming him too old for the provinces yet wanting him to enjoy their honor, never let him leave.

sentences.zh: 遷司徒公，侍中如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Duke of the Secretariat, retaining Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Duke of the Secretariat, still Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 就宅拜之。

translations.literal: The appointment was made at his residence.
translations.idiomatic: He was invested at home.

sentences.zh: 靈太后、明帝率百僚幸其第，宴會極歡。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling and Emperor Ming with the hundred officials visited his house and feasted to the full.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager and Emperor Ming led the court to his mansion for a feast of rare splendor.

sentences.zh: 又追京兆郡君為秦太上君。

translations.literal: Lady of Jingzhao Commandery was further posthumously made Grand August Lady of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Lady of Jingzhao was further raised posthumously to Grand August Lady of Qin.

sentences.zh: 太上君景明三年薨于洛陽，於此十六年矣。

translations.literal: The Grand August Lady had died at Luoyang in the third year of Jingming; sixteen years had now passed.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand August Lady had died at Luoyang in Jingming 3; sixteen years had passed.

sentences.zh: 太后乙太上君墳瘞卑局，更增廣，為起塋域門闕碑表。

translations.literal: The empress dowager, grieving that the Grand August Lady's tomb was low and cramped, enlarged it and raised tomb precinct gates, steles, and tables.
translations.idiomatic: Finding her mother's grave too mean, the empress dowager widened the mound and added gates, steles, and memorial tablets.

sentences.zh: 侍中崔光等奏：「按漢高祖母始諡曰昭靈夫人，後為昭靈後；

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Cui Guang and others memorialized: "By precedent Han Gaozu's grandmother was first titled Lady Zhaoling, later Lady Zhaoling the Late;
translations.idiomatic: Cui Guang and others wrote: "Han Gaozu's grandmother was first Lady Zhaoling, later Lady Zhaoling the Late;

sentences.zh: 薄太后母曰靈文夫人，皆置園邑三百家，長丞奉守。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Bo's mother was titled Lady Lingwen, and in each case three hundred households in a park estate with a chief and assistant were set to guard the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Bo's mother was Lady Lingwen; each had three hundred park households with wardens to tend the tomb.

sentences.zh: 今秦太上君未有尊諡，陵寢孤立，即秦君名，宜上終稱，兼設掃衛，以慰情典。

translations.literal: Now the Grand August Lady of Qin has no exalted posthumous title; her tomb stands alone—using the Qin Lady's name, a final title should be granted and guardians appointed to satisfy ritual feeling.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand August Lady of Qin lacks a final title and her tomb has no guard; we ask a closing title and caretakers to meet ritual need.

sentences.zh: 請上尊諡曰孝穆，權置園邑三十戶，立長丞奉守。」

translations.literal: We ask that the exalted posthumous title be Xiaomu, and for the present thirty park households with chief and assistant be set to guard the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: We propose the posthumous title Xiaomu and thirty park households with wardens for now.

sentences.zh: 太后從之。

translations.literal: The empress dowager assented.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager agreed.

sentences.zh: 封國珍繼室梁氏為趙平郡君。

translations.literal: Guozhen's second wife Lady Liang was enfeoffed Lady of Zhaoping Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen's second wife, Lady Liang, was made Lady of Zhaoping Commandery.

sentences.zh: 元叉妻拜為女侍中，封新平郡君，又徙封馮翊君。

translations.literal: Yuan Cha's wife was made Lady Attendant Within, enfeoffed Lady of Xinping Commandery, then transferred to Lady of Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Cha's wife became Lady Attendant Within, Lady of Xinping, then Lady of Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 國珍子祥妻長安縣公主，即清河王懌女也。

translations.literal: Guozhen's son Xiang's wife was Princess of Chang'an county—daughter of Prince of Qinghe Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang's wife was the Princess of Chang'an, daughter of Prince Yi of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 國珍年雖篤老，而雅敬佛法，時事潔齊，自禮拜。

translations.literal: Though Guozhen was deep in years, he revered the Buddhist Law and kept affairs of the time scrupulously clean, performing obeisance himself.
translations.idiomatic: Though aged, Guozhen honored the Dharma, kept his household in ritual order, and bowed with his own hands.

sentences.zh: 至於出入侍從，猶能跨馬據鞍。

translations.literal: Even in going out and attending with followers he could still mount a horse and sit the saddle.
translations.idiomatic: Going abroad with attendants, he could still mount and ride.

sentences.zh: 神龜元年四月七日，步從所建佛像，發第至閶闔門四五里。

translations.literal: On the seventh day of the fourth month of the first year of Shengui he walked from his house following the Buddha image he had built, four or five li to Changhe Gate.
translations.idiomatic: On Shengui 1.4.7 he walked from his mansion beside a Buddha image he had raised four or five li to Changhe Gate.

sentences.zh: 八日，又立觀像，晚乃肯坐。

translations.literal: On the eighth he again stood viewing the image and only at evening would sit.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighth he stood again before the image and would not sit until night.

sentences.zh: 勞熱增甚，因遂寢疾。

translations.literal: Fatigue and heat increased; he then took to his bed ill.
translations.idiomatic: Weariness and fever grew; he fell ill.

sentences.zh: 靈太后親侍藥膳，十二日薨，年八十。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling personally attended his medicines and food; on the twelfth he died, aged eighty.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager herself tended his medicines; on the twelfth he died at eighty.

sentences.zh: 給東園溫明秘器，五時朝服各一具，衣一襲，贈布五千匹，錢一百萬，蠟千斤。

translations.literal: He was given the Eastern Garden's warm bright secret coffin, one suit of court dress for each of the five seasons, one set of robes, five thousand bolts of cloth, a million cash, and a thousand jin of wax.
translations.idiomatic: He received the Eastern Garden coffin, seasonal court robes, a full suit, five thousand bolts of cloth, a million cash, and a thousand jin of wax.

sentences.zh: 大鴻臚持節監護喪事。

translations.literal: The Grand Herald, bearing the staff, supervised the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Herald supervised the rites with the staff of authority.

sentences.zh: 太后還宮，成服于九龍殿，遂居九龍寢室。

translations.literal: The empress dowager returned to the palace and put on mourning in the Hall of Nine Dragons, then dwelt in the Nine Dragons bedchamber.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager returned, mourned in the Hall of Nine Dragons, and lodged in the Nine Dragons chamber.

sentences.zh: 明帝服小功服，舉哀於太極東堂。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming wore the five-month mourning and gave lament in the east hall of the Imperial Ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming wore lesser mourning and wept in the east hall of Taiji.

sentences.zh: 又詔，自始薨至七七，皆為設千僧齋，齋令七人出家，百日設萬人齋，二七人出家。

translations.literal: An edict also ordered that from the first day of mourning to the forty-ninth day a thousand-monk feast be held each day, with seven men leaving home at each feast; at a hundred days a ten-thousand-monk feast, with twenty-seven leaving home.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts ordered thousand-monk feasts daily until the forty-ninth day, seven tonsured at each, and at a hundred days a feast for ten thousand monks with twenty-seven tonsured.

sentences.zh: 先是巫覡言將有凶，勸令為厭勝法，國珍拒而不從，雲吉凶有定分，唯修德以禳之。

translations.literal: Earlier a shaman had said there would be misfortune and urged apotropaic rites; Guozhen refused, saying fortune and misfortune have their allotted share—only cultivate virtue to avert them.
translations.idiomatic: A shaman had foretold ill luck and urged rites of expiation; Guozhen refused, saying fate is fixed and only virtue avails.

sentences.zh: 臨死，與太后訣，云「母子善臨天下」，殷勤至於再三。

translations.literal: At his death he took leave of the empress dowager, saying "Mother and son must govern the realm well," earnestly repeating it again and again.
translations.idiomatic: Dying, he told the empress dowager, "Mother and son must rule the realm well," again and again.

sentences.zh: 又及其子祥雲，「我唯有一子，死後勿如比來威抑之」。

translations.literal: He also spoke of his son Xiang, saying, "I have only this one son; after my death do not restrain him as of late."
translations.idiomatic: Of his son Xiang he said, "I have but one son; do not curb him as you have."

sentences.zh: 靈太后以其好戲，時加威訓，國珍故以為言。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling, because he loved play, often sternly admonished him—hence Guozhen's words.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager, vexed by Xiang's love of sport, had often rebuked him—hence the plea.

sentences.zh: 始國珍欲就祖、父，西葬舊鄉。

translations.literal: At first Guozhen wished to follow his grandfather and father and be buried in the old homeland to the west.
translations.idiomatic: At first he wished to bury his forebears in the western homeland.

sentences.zh: 後緣前世諸胡多在洛葬，有終洛之心。

translations.literal: Later, because former generations of many Hu had been buried at Luoyang, he came to favor ending at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Later, seeing how many barbarian houses of old lay at Luoyang, he inclined to remain there.

sentences.zh: 崔光嘗對太后前問國珍：「國公萬年後，為在此安厝？

translations.literal: Cui Guang once before the empress dowager asked Guozhen: "After ten thousand years, will the Duke be laid to rest here?
translations.idiomatic: Cui Guang once asked him before the empress dowager, "When you are gone, will you rest here

sentences.zh: 為歸長安？」

translations.literal: Or return to Chang'an?
translations.idiomatic: or return to Chang'an?

sentences.zh: 國珍言：「當陪葬天子山陵。」

translations.literal: Guozhen said, "I shall be buried with the Son of Heaven on the imperial hill."
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen answered, "I shall share the Son of Heaven's hill tomb."

sentences.zh: 及病危，太后請以後事，竟言還安定。

translations.literal: When his illness was grave the empress dowager asked his last wishes; he finally said to return to Anding.
translations.idiomatic: At the crisis the empress dowager asked his will; at last he said Anding.

sentences.zh: 語遂惛忽。

translations.literal: His words then grew confused.
translations.idiomatic: His speech then wandered.

sentences.zh: 太后問清河王懌與崔光等，議去留。

translations.literal: The empress dowager asked Prince of Qinghe Yi and Cui Guang and others to debate staying or going.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager asked Yi of Qinghe, Cui Guang, and others whether to stay or go.

sentences.zh: 懌等皆以病亂，請從先言。

translations.literal: Yi and the others all said that in the disorder of illness they should follow his earlier words.
translations.idiomatic: Yi and the rest, citing his delirium, urged his earlier wish.

sentences.zh: 太后猶記崔光昔與國珍言，遂營墓於洛陽。

translations.literal: The empress dowager still remembered Cui Guang's former talk with Guozhen and therefore had the tomb made at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: She recalled Guang's old question and had the tomb built at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 太后雖外從眾議，而深追臨終之語，云：「我公之遠慕二親，亦吾之思父母也。」

translations.literal: Though outwardly she followed the multitude's view, inwardly she deeply mourned his dying words, saying, "My lord's longing for his two parents is also my longing for my parents.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly she bowed to the court; inwardly she grieved his last words: "His yearning for his parents is mine for mine.

sentences.zh: 追崇假黃鉞、使持節、侍中、相國、都督中外諸軍事、太師，領太尉公、司州牧，號太上秦公，加九錫，葬以殊禮。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given the false Yellow Axe, Bearer of the Staff, Palace Attendant, Chancellor, Supervisor of Military Affairs Within and Without, Grand Preceptor, retaining Duke of the Grand Marshal and Governor of Sizhou, titled Grand August Lord of Qin, with the Nine Bestowals, and buried with extraordinary rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously given the yellow axe and staff, made chancellor and supreme commander, Grand Preceptor and Grand Marshal of Sizhou, titled Grand August Lord of Qin with the Nine Bestowals and a burial beyond ordinary measure.

sentences.zh: 給九旒鑾輅，武賁班劍百人，前後部羽葆鼓吹，巉輬車，諡曰文宣公。

translations.literal: He was given the nine tassels, imperial carriage, a hundred Tiger Guards with swords, front and rear feathered canopies and drums, a bier carriage, posthumous title Duke Wenxuan.
translations.idiomatic: He received the nine regalia, imperial equipage, a hundred guards, full honors of march, and the posthumous name Wenxuan.

sentences.zh: 賜物三千段，粟一千五百石。

translations.literal: Three thousand lengths of goods were granted and fifteen hundred shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Three thousand bolts of goods and fifteen hundred shi of grain were granted.

sentences.zh: 又詔贈國珍祖父、父，兄下逮從子，皆有封職。

translations.literal: An edict also posthumously enfeoffed Guozhen's grandfather, father, elder brother, and down to his cousins—all received offices.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts enfeoffed his grandfather, father, brother, and cousins as well.

sentences.zh: 持節就安定監護喪事。

translations.literal: A bearer of the staff went to Anding to supervise the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: A staff-bearer supervised the funeral in Anding.

sentences.zh: 靈太后迎太上君神柩還第，與國珍俱葬，贈襚一與國珍同。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling brought the Grand August Lady's coffin back to the residence and buried her with Guozhen, granting funeral goods equal to his.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager brought her mother's coffin home and buried her with Guozhen, with equal funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 及國珍神主入廟，詔太常權給以軒縣之樂，六佾之舞。

translations.literal: When Guozhen's spirit tablet entered the temple, an edict ordered the Minister of Rites provisionally to grant the xuan bell music and the six-row dance.
translations.idiomatic: When his tablet entered the ancestral temple, the Minister of Rites was told to grant xuan music and the six-row dance.

sentences.zh: 僧洗字湛輝，封爰德縣公，位中書監、侍中，改封濮陽郡公。

translations.literal: Sengxi, courtesy name Zhanhui, was enfeoffed Duke of Aide, made Supervisor of the Secretariat and Palace Attendant, then transferred to Duke of Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: Sengxi, styled Zhanhui, was Duke of Aide, then Supervisor of the Secretariat and Palace Attendant, then Duke of Puyang.

sentences.zh: 僧洗自永安後廢棄，不預朝政。

translations.literal: After Yongan, Sengxi was cast aside and took no part in court government.
translations.idiomatic: After Yongan he was set aside from government.

sentences.zh: 天平四年，薨。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianping he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Tianping 4.

sentences.zh: 詔給東園秘器，贈太師、太尉公、錄尚書事、雍州刺史，諡曰孝。

translations.literal: An edict granted the Eastern Garden secret coffin; posthumously he was made Grand Preceptor, Duke of the Grand Marshal, Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, and Governor of Yongzhou, posthumous title Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: He received the Eastern Garden coffin and posthumous honors as Grand Preceptor, Grand Marshal, supervisor of the Masters of Writing, and Governor of Yongzhou, titled Xiao.

sentences.zh: 真長子甯，字惠歸，襲國珍先爵，改為臨涇伯，後進為公。

translations.literal: Zhen's eldest son Ning, courtesy name Huigui, inherited Guozhen's former title, changed to Marquis of Linjing, later advanced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's eldest son Ning, styled Huigui, inherited the old title as Marquis of Linjing, later duke.

sentences.zh: 曆岐涇二州刺史，卒，諡曰孝穆。

translations.literal: He served in succession as Governor of Qi and Jing provinces and died, posthumous title Xiaomu.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Qi and Jing in turn, died, and was titled Xiaomu.

sentences.zh: 女為清河王亶妃，生孝靜皇帝。

translations.literal: His daughter was consort to Prince of Qinghe Chan and bore Emperor Xiaojing.
translations.idiomatic: His daughter married Prince Chan of Qinghe and bore Emperor Xiaojing.

sentences.zh: 武定初，贈太師、太尉公、錄尚書事，諡曰孝昭。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wuding he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor, Duke of the Grand Marshal, Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, posthumous title Xiaozhao.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wuding he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor, Grand Marshal, and supervisor of the Masters of Writing, titled Xiaozhao.

sentences.zh: 子虔，字僧敬。

translations.literal: His son Qian, courtesy name Sengjing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qian, styled Sengjing.

sentences.zh: 元叉之廢靈太后，虔時為千牛備身，與備身張車渠等謀叉。

translations.literal: When Yuan Cha deposed Empress Dowager Ling, Qian was Thousand-Ox Bodyguard and with Bodyguard Zhang Chequ and others plotted against Cha.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Cha ousted the empress dowager, Qian, a Thousand-Ox guardsman, plotted with Zhang Chequ and others to kill him.

sentences.zh: 事發，叉殺車渠等，虔坐遠徙。

translations.literal: The affair was exposed; Cha killed Chequ and the others, and Qian was banished far away.
translations.idiomatic: The plot failed; Cha executed Chequ and the rest and exiled Qian.

sentences.zh: 靈太后反政，徵為吏部郎中。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling returned to power he was summoned as Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress dowager regained power he was recalled as a director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 太后好以家人禮與親族宴戲，虔常致諫，由是，後宴謔多不預焉。

translations.literal: The empress dowager loved to feast with kin in family fashion; Qian often remonstrated, and thereafter she often left him out of her banter.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager loved private feasts with kin; Qian's remonstrances kept him from many of them.

sentences.zh: 出為涇州刺史，封安陽縣侯。

translations.literal: He went out as Governor of Jingzhou and was enfeoffed Marquis of Anyang.
translations.idiomatic: He became Governor of Jingzhou and Marquis of Anyang.

sentences.zh: 興和三年，以帝元舅，超遷司空公。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xinghe, as the emperor's maternal uncle by blood, he was promoted over rank to Duke of the Works.
translations.idiomatic: In Xinghe 3, as the emperor's uterine uncle, he leapt to Duke of the Works.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈太傅、太尉公、尚書僕射、徐州刺史，諡曰宣。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made Grand Tutor, Duke of the Grand Marshal, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and Governor of Xuzhou, posthumous title Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: On his death he was made Grand Tutor, Grand Marshal, vice director of the Masters of Writing, and Governor of Xuzhou, titled Xuan.

sentences.zh: 葬日，百官會葬，乘輿送于郭外。

translations.literal: On the day of burial the hundred officials attended the funeral and the imperial carriage saw him off beyond the outer wall.
translations.idiomatic: At his burial the whole court followed; the emperor's carriage went to the city gate.

sentences.zh: 子長粲。

translations.literal: His son Changcan.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Changcan.

sentences.zh: 長粲仕齊，累遷章武太守，為政清靜，頗得人和。

translations.literal: Changcan served Qi, rose in succession to Administrator of Zhangwu, and in government was quiet and pure, winning the people's regard.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qi he rose to Administrator of Zhangwu; his rule was quiet and fair and won the people.

sentences.zh: 除兼併省尚書左丞，當官正色，無所回避。

translations.literal: He was made Acting Left Director in the Combined Ministry and in office showed a stern countenance, yielding to none.
translations.idiomatic: Made acting left director in the combined ministry, he showed a stern face and yielded to none.

sentences.zh: 尚書左僕射趙彥深密勿樞要，中書舍人裴澤便蕃左右，以殿門受拜，皆彈糾之。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director Zhao Yanshen held secret control of the pivot, and Secretariat Attendant Pei Ze was intimate at the emperor's side; for receiving obeisance at the Hall Gate Changcan impeached them both.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Zhao Yanshen, who held the inner pivot, and Pei Ze, favorite at the emperor's side, for bowing at the hall gate.

sentences.zh: 彥深等頗有恨言，長粲不以介意。

translations.literal: Yanshen and the others bore considerable resentment, but Changcan paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshen and the rest resented it; Changcan did not care.

sentences.zh: 後主踐祚，長粲被敕，與黃門馮子琮出入禁中，專典敷奏。

translations.literal: When the later sovereign ascended, Changcan was ordered with Huangmen Feng Ziqiong to enter the forbidden precinct and specialize in drafting and memorials.
translations.idiomatic: The new emperor ordered Changcan and Feng Ziqiong of the Huangmen to draft memorials within the palace.

sentences.zh: 武成還鄴，後主在晉陽，長粲仍受委留後。

translations.literal: Wucheng returned to Ye; the later sovereign was at Jinyang—Changcan still received commission to remain and oversee affairs.
translations.idiomatic: While Wucheng was at Ye and the heir at Jinyang, Changcan stayed behind with power.

sentences.zh: 後主從武成還鄴，仍敕在京省判度支尚書，監議五禮。

translations.literal: When the later sovereign followed Wucheng back to Ye he was still ordered to judge the Revenue Ministry in the capital and supervise debate on the Five Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to Ye, he was told to judge revenue in the capital and oversee the Five Rites.

sentences.zh: 武成崩，與領軍婁定遠、錄尚書趙彥深、左僕射和士開、高文遙、領軍綦連猛、高阿那肱、右僕射唐邕，同知朝政，時人號為八貴。

translations.literal: When Wucheng died, with Commander-in-chief Lou Dingyuan, Recorder Zhao Yanshen, Left Vice Director He Shiqi, Gao Wenyao, Commander-in-chief Qilian Meng, Gao Anagong, and Right Vice Director Tang Yong he shared in court government; men of the time called them the Eight Dignitaries.
translations.idiomatic: At Wucheng's death he joined Lou Dingyuan, Zhao Yanshen, He Shiqi, Gao Wenyao, Qilian Meng, Gao Anagong, and Tang Yong in rule—the Eight Dignitaries.

sentences.zh: 于後定遠、文遙並出，唐邕專典外兵，綦連猛、高阿那肱別總武任，長粲常在左右，兼宣詔令。

translations.literal: Later Dingyuan and Wenyao went out; Tang Yong alone held outer troops; Qilian Meng and Gao Anagong separately held military posts; Changcan was always at the emperor's side and also proclaimed edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Dingyuan and Wenyao left; Tang Yong held the armies; Meng and Anagong held military posts; Changcan stayed at the emperor's side and proclaimed edicts.

sentences.zh: 從幸晉陽。

translations.literal: He followed on an excursion to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the court to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 後主既富於春秋，庶事皆相歸委。

translations.literal: The later sovereign, rich in years, entrusted him with the myriad affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The young emperor entrusted him with daily business.

sentences.zh: 長粲盡心毗奉，甚得名譽。

translations.literal: Changcan devoted himself in support and won a fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Changcan served with zeal and won praise.

sentences.zh: 又正為侍中。

translations.literal: He was again made regular Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was made full Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，給假馳驛奔喪。

translations.literal: When his mother died he was given leave and post-horses for swift return.
translations.idiomatic: On his mother's death he was given leave and relay horses.

sentences.zh: 尋有詔，起復前任。

translations.literal: Soon an edict recalled him to his former post before mourning ended.
translations.idiomatic: An edict soon recalled him from mourning.

sentences.zh: 隴東王長仁心欲入處機要之地，為執政不許。

translations.literal: Prince of Longdong Changren wished to enter a place of power in government, but the ministers would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Changren of Longdong sought a share in rule; the ministers refused.

sentences.zh: 長仁疑長粲通謀，大以為恨，言于太后，發其陰私，請出為州。

translations.literal: Changren suspected Changcan of plotting against him and greatly resented it; he spoke to the empress dowager, exposed his private faults, and asked that he be sent to a province.
translations.idiomatic: Changren thought Changcan blocked him; he told the empress dowager of private faults and asked him out to the provinces.

sentences.zh: 太后為言于後主，不獲已，從焉。

translations.literal: The empress dowager spoke for him to the later sovereign; unable to refuse, he consented.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager pleaded; the emperor yielded.

sentences.zh: 除趙州刺史。

translations.literal: He was made Governor of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent as Governor of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 及辭，眷戀流涕，後主亦憫然慰勉之。

translations.literal: At his farewell both were moved to tears; the later sovereign also comforted him with pity.
translations.idiomatic: At parting both wept; the emperor comforted him tenderly.

sentences.zh: 至州，存心政事，為人吏所懷。

translations.literal: In the province he kept his mind on government and was cherished by officials and people.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhao he minded governance and won officials and people alike.

sentences.zh: 因沐發，手不得舉，失瘖，卒於州。

translations.literal: While washing his hair his hands could not be raised; he lost his voice and died in the province.
translations.idiomatic: While bathing his arms failed; he lost speech and died in office.

sentences.zh: 後主聞而傷悼，在朝文武嗟歎，咸惜之。

translations.literal: When the later sovereign heard, he grieved; civil and military at court sighed and all mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grieved; courtiers sighed and mourned.

sentences.zh: 贈司空公、尚書左僕射、瀛州刺史，諡文貞公。

translations.literal: Posthumously made Duke of the Works, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and Governor of Yingzhou, posthumous title Duke Wen the Upright.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously Duke of the Works, left vice director, and Governor of Yingzhou, titled Wen the Upright.

sentences.zh: 長粲性溫雅，在官清潔。

translations.literal: Changcan was mild and elegant in nature and pure in office.
translations.idiomatic: Changcan was gentle, elegant, and clean in office.

sentences.zh: 但始居要密，便為子叔泉取清河王崔德儉女為妻。

translations.literal: But as soon as he reached a secret post of power he took Cui Dejian's daughter as wife for his nephew Shuiquan.
