translations.idiomatic: Yet once in power he married his nephew Shuiquan to Cui Dejian's daughter of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 在晉陽處分，用妻弟王逖與德儉對為司徒主簿，時論以此譏之。

translations.literal: While disposing affairs at Jinyang he made his wife's younger brother Wang Ti and Dejian reciprocal chief clerks of the Secretariat—on this account opinion reproached him.
translations.idiomatic: At Jinyang he paired his wife's brother Wang Ti with Dejian as Secretariat clerks, which drew censure.

sentences.zh: 又性好內。

translations.literal: He also loved women within the household.
translations.idiomatic: He was also fond of women indoors.

sentences.zh: 有一侍婢，其妻王驕妒，手刺殺之，為此忿恨，數年不相見。

translations.literal: He had a serving maid whom his wife Wang, proud and jealous, stabbed to death; for this he bore resentment and for years did not see her.
translations.idiomatic: A maid he favored was stabbed by his jealous wife Wang; he resented it and did not see her for years.

sentences.zh: 親表為之語曰：「自我不見，於今三年。」

translations.literal: Kin composed a saying for them: "Since I last saw you, three years have passed.
translations.idiomatic: Kin quoted for them, "Since I saw you last, three years have passed.

sentences.zh: 後納妾李氏，仍與王氏別宅，亦無朝拜之禮。

translations.literal: Later he took concubine Lady Li and lived in a separate house from Lady Wang, with no courtesies of bowing between them.
translations.idiomatic: Later he took Lady Li as concubine and lived apart from Wang without ceremony.

sentences.zh: 嫠婦公孫氏也，已殺三夫，長粲不信，強取之，令與李氏同住，未期而亡。

translations.literal: There was also the widow Lady Gongsun, who had already killed three husbands; Changcan did not believe it and forced her to him, placing her with Lady Li; before the term was out she died.
translations.idiomatic: He also seized the widow Gongsun, who had buried three husbands, and set her with Lady Li; she soon died.

sentences.zh: 子仲操，位陳留太守。

translations.literal: His son Zhongcao held the post of Administrator of Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhongcao was Administrator of Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 次叔泉，通直散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: The second son Shuiquan was Regular Attendant and Cavalier Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Shuiquan was regular and cavalier attendant.

sentences.zh: 先是，望氣者上言，太白食昴，法當大赦。

translations.literal: Earlier a diviner of the heavens had reported that the White Planet would eclipse Mao; by rule there should be a great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: A sky-watcher said the White Planet would eclipse Mao, portending a great amnesty.

sentences.zh: 和士開奏聞，詔降罪人以應之。

translations.literal: He Shiqi reported it; an edict reduced punishments on criminals to answer the omen.
translations.idiomatic: He Shiqi told the throne; criminals' sentences were eased to match the sign.

sentences.zh: 尚書左僕射徐之才諳練往事，語士開曰：「天垂象，見吉凶，有成災者，有不成災者。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director Xu Zhicai, versed in past affairs, said to Shiqi: "Heaven shows images to reveal fortune and misfortune; some omens bring disaster, some do not.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhicai, versed in precedent, told Shiqi, "Heaven's signs show fortune or ill; some fulfill disaster, some do not.

sentences.zh: 案昴，趙分，或云趙地有災。

translations.literal: Mao is the allotment of Zhao; some say disaster will strike Zhao lands.
translations.idiomatic: Mao is Zhao's field; some say Zhao will suffer.

sentences.zh: 古者，王侯各在封邑，故分野有災，當其君長。

translations.literal: In antiquity kings and marquises each dwelt in their fiefs, so when an allotment suffered disaster it fell on its lord.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity lords dwelt in their fiefs; when a field suffered, its lord did.

sentences.zh: 今吾等虛名，竟不之國。

translations.literal: Now we bear empty titles and in the end do not go to our states.
translations.idiomatic: Today we hold empty titles and never rule our lands.

sentences.zh: 刺史專令一境，善惡所歸，比來多以刺史為驗。」

translations.literal: A governor alone commands one region; good and evil return to him—in recent times many have taken the governor as the test.
translations.idiomatic: A governor alone holds a circuit; merit and fault settle on him—lately men watch governors.

sentences.zh: 未幾而長粲死焉。

translations.literal: Before long Changcan died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, Changcan died.

sentences.zh: 甯弟盛，字歸興，位左衛將軍，賜爵江陽男。

translations.literal: Ning's younger brother Sheng, courtesy name Guixing, was Left Guards General and enfeoffed Baron of Jiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ning's younger brother Sheng, styled Guixing, was Left Guards General and Baron of Jiangyang.

sentences.zh: 曆幽、瀛二州刺史，為政清靜，人吏愛之。

translations.literal: He served in succession as Governor of You and Ying provinces; in government he was quiet and pure and officials and people loved him.
translations.idiomatic: He governed You and Ying in turn, quietly and fairly, and was loved.

sentences.zh: 轉冀州刺史，卒，賜司徒公、錄尚書事、定州刺史，追封陽平郡公，諡曰懿穆。

translations.literal: Transferred to Governor of Jizhou, he died; granted Duke of the Secretariat, Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, and Governor of Dingzhou, posthumously enfeoffed Duke of Yangping, posthumous title Yimu the Reverent.
translations.idiomatic: Made Governor of Jizhou, he died; honored as duke of the Secretariat, supervisor, and Governor of Dingzhou, enfeoffed posthumously as Duke of Yangping, titled Yimu the Reverent.

sentences.zh: 明帝后納其女為皇太后。

translations.literal: Later Emperor Ming took his daughter as empress, who became empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming his daughter was raised to empress and then empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 太后舅皇甫集，字元會，一字文都，安定朝那人。

translations.literal: The empress dowager's maternal uncle Huangfu Ji, courtesy name Yuanhui, also styled Wendu, was a man of Zhaoning in Anding.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager's uncle Huangfu Ji, styled Yuanhui and Wendu, came from Zhaoning in Anding.

sentences.zh: 封涇陽縣公，位儀同三司、雍州刺史、右衛大將軍，贈侍中、司空公，諡曰靜。

translations.literal: Enfeoffed Duke of Jingyang, made Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, Governor of Yongzhou, and Right Guards General; posthumously Palace Attendant, Duke of the Works, posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He was Duke of Jingyang, equal to the three excellencies, Governor of Yongzhou, and Right Guards General; posthumously Palace Attendant and Duke of the Works, titled Jing.

sentences.zh: 集弟度，字文亮，封安縣公，累遷尚書左僕射，領左衛將軍。

translations.literal: Ji's younger brother Du, courtesy name Wenliang, was enfeoffed Duke of An, rose in succession to Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Commander of the Left Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's younger brother Du, styled Wenliang, was Duke of An and rose to left vice director and commander of the left guards.

sentences.zh: 度頑蔽，每與人言，自稱僕射，時人方之毛嘉。

translations.literal: Du was dull and obstructive; whenever he spoke with others he called himself Vice Director—men of the time compared him to Mao Jia.
translations.idiomatic: Du was obtuse; in conversation he called himself Vice Director—men compared him to Mao Jia.

sentences.zh: 正光初，元叉出之為都督、瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguang Yuan Cha sent him out as Supervisor and Governor of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguang Yuan Cha sent him out as supervisor and Governor of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 度不願出，頻表固辭，乃除右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Du did not wish to go and repeatedly memorialized firm refusal; he was therefore made Right Counselor of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Du refused and memorialized again and again; he was made Right Counselor of the Palace instead.

sentences.zh: 孝昌元年，為司空、領軍將軍，加侍中。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiaochang he was made Minister of Works, Commander-in-chief, and Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaochang 1 he was Minister of Works, commander-in-chief, and Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 元叉之見出也，恐朝夕誅滅，度與妻陳氏，多納其貨，為之左右。

translations.literal: When Yuan Cha was driven out he feared execution morning and evening; Du and his wife Lady Chen took much of his goods and worked at his side.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Cha fell, Du and his wife Chen took his bribes and pleaded for him.

sentences.zh: 度無子，養兄集子子熙為子。

translations.literal: Du had no son and adopted his elder brother Ji's son Zixi as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Childless, Du adopted Ji's son Zixi.

sentences.zh: 子熙嫂趙郡太守裴佗女。

translations.literal: Zixi's wife was daughter of Administrator of Zhao Pei Tuo.
translations.idiomatic: Zixi's wife was Pei Tuo's daughter, Zhao's administrator.

sentences.zh: 佗還京師，度問佗外何消息，佗曰：「行路所聞，唯道明公多取元叉金帛，遠近無不慨歎。

translations.literal: When Tuo returned to the capital Du asked what news he had from outside; Tuo said: "On the road one hears only that the Illustrious Duke took much gold and silk from Yuan Cha—near and far all sigh.
translations.idiomatic: Tuo returning, Du asked the news abroad; Tuo said, "Travelers say the Illustrious Duke took Yuan Cha's gold and silk—everyone sighs.

sentences.zh: 公宜戮此罪人，以謝天下。」

translations.literal: You ought to kill this criminal to answer the realm.
translations.idiomatic: You should slay that villain to appease the realm.

sentences.zh: 陳氏聞而惡之。

translations.literal: Lady Chen heard and hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Chen heard and hated Tuo.

sentences.zh: 又攝吏部事，遷司徒，兼尚書令，不拜。

translations.literal: He also held acting charge of the Ministry of Personnel, was transferred to Grand Marshal, and concurrently Director of the Masters of Writing, but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He also acted in Personnel, then Grand Marshal and director of the Masters of Writing, which he refused.

sentences.zh: 尋轉太尉，孜孜營利，老而彌甚。

translations.literal: Soon transferred to Grand Preceptor, he zealously sought profit, more so in old age.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Grand Preceptor, he grasped for gain ever more in age.

sentences.zh: 遷授之際，皆自請乞。

translations.literal: At each transfer he begged the posts himself.
translations.idiomatic: At every promotion he begged the office.

sentences.zh: 靈太后知其無用。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling knew he was useless.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager knew him worthless.

sentences.zh: 以舅氏，難違之。

translations.literal: As a maternal uncle she found it hard to refuse him.
translations.idiomatic: As her uncle she could not refuse.

sentences.zh: 然所曆官，最為貪蠹。

translations.literal: Yet among the offices he held he was most greedy and corrupt.
translations.idiomatic: Yet of all offices his was the greediest.

sentences.zh: 爾硃榮入洛，西奔兄子華州刺史邕，尋與邕為人所殺。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang he fled west to his nephew Yong, Governor of Huazhou, and soon he and Yong were killed by others.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong took Luoyang he fled to his nephew Yong, Governor of Huazhou, and both were killed.

sentences.zh: 楊騰，弘農人，文帝之舅也。

translations.literal: Yang Teng was a man of Hongnong and maternal uncle to Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Teng of Hongnong was Emperor Wen's uncle.

sentences.zh: 父貴，琅邪郡守，封華陰男。

translations.literal: His father Gui was Administrator of Langye and enfeoffed Baron of Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gui was Langye's administrator and Baron of Huayin.

sentences.zh: 騰妹為京兆王愉妃，故騰得處貴遊。

translations.literal: Teng's younger sister was consort to Prince of Jingzhao Yu, and so Teng came to move among the noble.
translations.idiomatic: His sister was Prince Yu of Jingzhao's consort, and Teng rose among the great.

sentences.zh: 景明初，襲爵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingming he inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingming he inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 後為襄城太守，甚有聲稱。

translations.literal: Later he was Administrator of Xiangcheng and won a fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Later he governed Xiangcheng with a fine name.

sentences.zh: 文帝即位，位開府儀同三司，出鎮河東。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen ascended he was made Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies with an established staff and went out to hold Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: At Wen's accession he was equal to the three excellencies with a staff and held Hedong.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈司空、雍州刺史，諡曰貞襄。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made Minister of Works and Governor of Yongzhou, posthumous title Zhenxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He died posthumously Minister of Works and Governor of Yongzhou, titled Zhenxiang.

sentences.zh: 子盛。

translations.literal: His son Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Sheng.

sentences.zh: 乙弗繪，河南洛陽人，文帝皇后之兄也。

translations.literal: Yifu Hui was a man of Luoyang in Henan and elder brother to Emperor Wen's empress.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu Hui of Luoyang in Henan was the empress's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 文帝即位，位開府儀同三司、侍中、中書監、魏昌縣公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen ascended he was made Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, Palace Attendant, Supervisor of the Secretariat, and Duke of Weichang.
translations.idiomatic: At Wen's accession he was equal to the three excellencies, Palace Attendant, supervisor of the Secretariat, and Duke of Weichang.

sentences.zh: 又為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was also Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He also directed the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 趙猛，太安狄那人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Meng was a man of Dina in Tai'an.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Meng came from Dina in Tai'an.

sentences.zh: 姊為齊文穆皇帝繼室，生趙郡公琛。

translations.literal: His elder sister was the successor consort of Emperor Wenmu of Qi and bore Duke Chen of Zhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His sister was Qi Wenmu's successor consort and bore Duke Chen of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 猛性方直，頗有器幹。

translations.literal: Meng was square and upright by nature and had considerable capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Meng was upright and capable.

sentences.zh: 齊神武舉義，以預義勳，封信都縣伯。

translations.literal: When Qi Shenwu raised the righteous standard he was enfeoffed for merit in the cause as Baron of Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenwu raised the banner of revolt, Meng was enfeoffed Baron of Xindu for his part.

sentences.zh: 累遷南營州刺史。

translations.literal: He rose in succession to Governor of Southern Camp.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Governor of Southern Camp.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈司空公。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made Duke of the Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died posthumously Duke of the Works.

sentences.zh: 胡長仁，字孝隆，安定臨涇人，齊武成皇后長兄也。

translations.literal: Hu Changren, courtesy name Xiaolong, was a man of Linting in Anding and elder brother to Empress Wu of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Changren of Linting in Anding, styled Xiaolong, was Empress Wu's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 父延之，魏中書令、兗州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Yanzhi was Secretariat Director and Governor of Yanzhou under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yanzhi had been Wei's Secretariat Director and Governor of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 大寧中，贈司空公。

translations.literal: In the Daning era he was posthumously made Duke of the Works.
translations.idiomatic: In Daning his father was posthumously Duke of the Works.

sentences.zh: 長仁以內戚，歷位尚書左僕射、尚書令。

translations.literal: As inner kin Changren rose to Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: As imperial kin he became left vice director and director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 及武成崩，預參朝政，封隴東郡王。

translations.literal: When Wucheng died he took part in court government and was enfeoffed Prince of Longdong.
translations.idiomatic: At Wucheng's death he shared in rule and was made Prince of Longdong.

sentences.zh: 左丞酈孝裕、郎中陸仁惠、盧元亮厚相結讬。

translations.literal: Left Assistant Director Li Xiaoyu, Director Li Renhui, and Lu Yuanliang thickly banded together with him.
translations.idiomatic: Left assistant Li Xiaoyu, director Li Renhui, and Lu Yuanliang clung to him.

sentences.zh: 長仁每上省，孝裕必方駕而來。

translations.literal: Whenever Changren went up to the ministry, Xiaoyu always came in matched carriages.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Changren entered the ministry, Xiaoyu came in paired carriages.

sentences.zh: 省務既繁，簿案堆積，令史欲諮都坐者，日有百數。

translations.literal: Provincial business was already heavy and documents piled up; clerks wishing to consult the chief seat numbered a hundred each day.
translations.idiomatic: Paperwork piled high; a hundred clerks a day sought the chief seat.

sentences.zh: 孝裕屏人私話，朝退亦相隨。

translations.literal: Xiaoyu screened others for private talk and after court still followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyu dismissed others for private talk and followed him after court.

sentences.zh: 仁惠、元亮又伺閑而往，停斷公事，人號為三佞。

translations.literal: Renhui and Yuanliang also waited on his leisure and went; they interrupted public business—people called them the Three Sycophants.
translations.idiomatic: Renhui and Yuanliang seized his idle hours and halted business—men called them the Three Sycophants.

sentences.zh: 長仁私遊仄密，處處追尋。

translations.literal: Changren privately roamed in narrow secrecy, pursuing him everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Changren pursued secret pleasures and tracked him everywhere.

sentences.zh: 孝裕勸其求進，和士開深疾之，於是奏除孝裕為章武郡守，元亮為淮南郡守，仁惠為幽州長史。

translations.literal: Xiaoyu urged him to seek advancement; He Shiqi deeply hated this and therefore memorialized to remove Xiaoyu as Administrator of Zhangwu, Yuanliang as Administrator of Huainan, and Renhui as Chief Clerk of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyu urged his rise; He Shiqi hated it and had Xiaoyu sent to Zhangwu, Yuanliang to Huainan, Renhui to You as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 孝裕又說長仁曰：「王陽臥疾，和士開必來，因而殺之。

translations.literal: Xiaoyu also said to Changren: "When Wang Yang lies ill, He Shiqi is sure to come—then kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyu also told Changren, "When Wang Yang feigns illness, He Shiqi will come—kill him then.

sentences.zh: 入見太后，不過百日失官，便代其處。」

translations.literal: Enter and see the empress dowager; within a hundred days you will lose office and take his place.
translations.idiomatic: See the empress dowager; within a hundred days you will lose office and take his.

sentences.zh: 士開知其謀，更徙孝裕為北營州建德郡守。

translations.literal: Shiqi learned of the plot and transferred Xiaoyu again to Administrator of Jiande in Northern Campzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi learned the plot and sent Xiaoyu to Jiande in Northern Campzhou.

sentences.zh: 長仁每幹執事，求為領軍。

translations.literal: Changren often interfered in those who held affairs, asking to be Commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Changren often pressed those in power for the commander-in-chief's post.

sentences.zh: 將相文武以主上富於春秋，母后家不可專政，故抑而不許。

translations.literal: Civil and military ministers, because the sovereign was rich in years and the empress's kin must not monopolize government, therefore checked and did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers, saying the emperor was young and maternal kin must not rule alone, refused.

sentences.zh: 以本官攝選。

translations.literal: He held selection affairs in his regular post.
translations.idiomatic: He held selection in his regular office.

sentences.zh: 長仁性好威福，意猶未盡。

translations.literal: Changren loved power and favor and his intent was still not satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: Changren loved power; his wish was still unsated.

sentences.zh: 先是尚書胡長粲奏事內省，長仁疑粲間己，苦請太后出之。

translations.literal: Earlier Director Hu Changcan had reported affairs in the inner court; Changren suspected Changcan was against him and urgently asked the empress dowager to send him out.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Hu Changcan had reported within the palace; Changren thought him hostile and begged the empress dowager to send him out.

sentences.zh: 天統五年，從駕自並還鄴，夜發滏口，帝以夜漏尚早，停于路傍。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tiantong, following the emperor from Bing back to Ye, they set out at night from Fukou; the emperor, because the night watch was still early, halted by the road.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiantong 5, returning from Bing to Ye, they left Fukou at night; the emperor halted early on the road.

sentences.zh: 長仁後來，謂是從行諸貴，遂遣門客程牙馳騎呼問。

translations.literal: Changren came later, took them for the nobles following, and sent his gate guest Cheng Ya galloping on horseback to call and ask.
translations.idiomatic: Changren came after, mistook them for the following nobles, and sent Cheng Ya to gallop and call.

sentences.zh: 帝遣中尚食陳德信問是何人，牙不答而走。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Palace Provisioner Chen Dexin to ask who it was; Ya did not answer and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Chen Dexin to ask who it was; Ya fled without answer.

sentences.zh: 帝命左右追射之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered his attendants to pursue and shoot.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered pursuit and arrows.

sentences.zh: 既而捉獲，因令壯士撲之，決馬鞭二百，牙一宿便死。

translations.literal: They were soon seized; he then ordered stout men to beat him, two hundred strokes of the horse whip decided, and Ya died in one night.
translations.idiomatic: Seized, stout men beat him two hundred strokes with the horsewhip; Ya died overnight.

sentences.zh: 士開因此，遂令德信列長仁倚親驕豪無畏憚。

translations.literal: Shiqi therefore had Dexin list Changren's relying on kinship, arrogant and fearless.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi had Dexin list Changren's arrogance as kin.

sentences.zh: 由是，除齊州刺史。

translations.literal: On this account he was made Governor of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Governor of Qi.

sentences.zh: 及辭于昭陽，列仗引見，長仁不敢發語，唯泣涕橫流。

translations.literal: At his farewell in Zhaoyang, ranks of guards led him in to audience; Changren dared not speak, only weeping in streams.
translations.idiomatic: At farewell in Zhaoyang, guards led him in; he only wept.

sentences.zh: 到任，啟求暫歸，所司不為奏。

translations.literal: Arriving in his province he memorialized asking brief return; the office did not report it.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi he asked brief leave; the office ignored it.

sentences.zh: 怨憤，謀令冀州人李揩牆刺和士開，其弟長咸告之。

translations.literal: Resentful, he plotted with a man of Jizhou, Li Kai, to have him stab He Shiqi on the wall; his younger brother Changxian reported it.
translations.idiomatic: In resentment he had Li Kai of Jizhou stab Shiqi on the wall; his brother Changxian informed.

sentences.zh: 士開密與祖孝徵議之，孝徵引漢文帝殺薄昭為故事，於是敕遣張固、劉桃枝馳驛詣齊州，責長仁謀害宰輔，遂賜死。

translations.literal: Shiqi secretly discussed with Zu Xiaozheng; Xiaozheng cited Han Wendi's killing of Bo Zhao as precedent, and therefore an edict sent Zhang Gu and Liu Taozhi post-horses to Qi, charged Changren with plotting to harm the chief minister, and granted death.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi and Zu Xiaozheng cited Han Wendi's killing of Bo Zhao; Zhang Gu and Liu Taozhi rode post-horses to Qi, charged murder of the chief minister, and granted death.

sentences.zh: 先是，太白食昴，占者曰：「昴為趙分，不利胡王。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when the White Planet eclipsed Mao, the diviner said: "Mao is the allotment of Zhao; ill for the Hu king.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the White Planet had eclipsed Mao; diviners said, "Mao is Zhao's field—ill for the Hu king.

sentences.zh: 長仁未幾死。

translations.literal: Before long Changren died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Changren died.

sentences.zh: 長仁性好歌舞，飲酒至數斗不亂。

translations.literal: Changren loved song and dance and drinking several dou without disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Changren loved song, dance, and drinking several dou without failing.

sentences.zh: 自至齊州，每進酒後，必長歎欷歔，流涕不自勝，左右莫不怪之。

translations.literal: From the time he reached Qi, after each round of wine he always sighed and wept, unable to master himself—those at his side all found it strange.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi, after each cup he sighed and wept beyond control—attendants marveled.

sentences.zh: 尋而後主納長仁女為後，重加贈。

translations.literal: Soon the later sovereign took Changren's daughter as empress and added posthumous honors.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the emperor took his daughter as empress and raised his honors.

sentences.zh: 長仁子君璧，襲爵隴東王。

translations.literal: Changren's son Junbi inherited the title Prince of Longdong.
translations.idiomatic: His son Junbi inherited Longdong.

sentences.zh: 君璧弟君璋，及長仁弟長雍等，前後七人並賜爵，合門貴盛。

translations.literal: Junbi's younger brother Junzhang, and Changren's younger brother Changyong and others—seven men in all before and after—were enfeoffed; the whole house was exalted.
translations.idiomatic: Junzhang, Changyong, and others—seven in all—were enfeoffed; the house flourished.

sentences.zh: 後廢後，稍稍黜退焉。

translations.literal: After the empress was deposed they were gradually demoted.
translations.idiomatic: After her deposition they were slowly pushed down.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝外家呂氏，其族蓋微。

translations.literal: The Lü clan, maternal kin to Emperor Wen of Sui, was by origin slight.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen's Lü kin were of humble stock.

sentences.zh: 平齊後求訪，不知所在。

translations.literal: After pacifying Qi they sought them but did not know where they were.
translations.idiomatic: After Qi fell they searched in vain.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，濟南郡上言，有男子呂永吉，自稱有姑字苦桃，嫁為楊諱妻。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, Jinan commandery reported a man Lü Yongji who said he had an aunt styled Kutao who had married a man surnamed Yang.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang, Jinan reported Lü Yongji, who said an aunt Kutao had married a Yang.

sentences.zh: 勘驗，知是舅子。

translations.literal: On investigation they knew he was the empress's nephew.
translations.idiomatic: Inquiry proved him the empress's nephew.

sentences.zh: 始追贈外祖雙周為上柱國、太尉、八州諸軍事、青州刺史，封齊郡公，諡曰敬。

translations.literal: Only then were the maternal grandfather Shuangzhou posthumously made Pillar of State, Grand Marshal, Supervisor of Military Affairs for Eight Provinces, and Governor of Qingzhou, enfeoffed Duke of Qi, posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Then maternal grandfather Shuangzhou was posthumously Pillar of State, Grand Marshal, commander of eight provinces, Governor of Qingzhou, Duke of Qi, titled Jing.

sentences.zh: 外祖母姚氏為齊敬公夫人。

translations.literal: The maternal grandmother Lady Yao was made Lady of Duke Jing of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Grandmother Lady Yao was Lady of Duke Jing of Qi.

sentences.zh: 詔並改葬，于齊州立廟，置守塚十家，以永吉襲爵，留在京師。

translations.literal: An edict also ordered reburial; a temple was raised in Qi with ten tomb-guard households; Yongji inherited the title and remained in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts ordered reburial, a temple in Qi with ten guardians; Yongji inherited and stayed at court.

sentences.zh: 及大業中，授上党郡太守。

translations.literal: In the Daye era he was made Administrator of Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: In Daye he was Administrator of Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 性識庸劣，職務不理。

translations.literal: His nature and knowledge were base and inferior; he did not manage his duties.
translations.idiomatic: He was dull and neglected office.

sentences.zh: 後去官，不知所終。

translations.literal: Later he left office and his end is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Later he left office; his end is unknown.

sentences.zh: 從父道貴，性尤頑騃，言詞鄙陋。

translations.literal: His paternal uncle Daogui was especially stupid and coarse, his words vulgar.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Daogui was brutish and spoke coarsely.

sentences.zh: 初自鄉里徵入長安，上見之悲泣。

translations.literal: When first summoned from the village into Chang'an the emperor saw him and wept.
translations.idiomatic: First summoned from the village, the emperor wept at sight of him.

sentences.zh: 道貴略無戚容，但連呼帝名云：「種未定不可偷，大似苦桃姊。」

translations.literal: Daogui showed hardly any grief but only kept calling the emperor's name, saying, "The seed is not yet fixed—you must not steal; you greatly resemble Sister Kutao.
translations.idiomatic: Daogui showed no grief but cried the emperor's name: "The seed is unsettled—do not steal; you look like Sister Kutao.

sentences.zh: 後數犯忌諱，動致違忤。

translations.literal: Later he often violated taboo and always met with offense.
translations.idiomatic: Later he broke taboo and often gave offense.

sentences.zh: 上甚恥之，乃命高熲厚加供給，不許接對朝士。

translations.literal: The emperor was deeply shamed and therefore ordered Gao Jiong to supply him richly and forbade him to meet court gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed, the emperor had Gao Jiong supply him richly and barred court access.

sentences.zh: 拜上儀同三司，出為濟南太守，令即之任，斷其入朝。

translations.literal: He was made Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies and sent out as Administrator of Jinan, ordered to go at once and cut off his entry to court.
translations.idiomatic: He was made equal to the three excellencies, sent to Jinan, and barred from court.

sentences.zh: 道貴還至本郡，高自崇重，每與人言，自稱皇舅。

translations.literal: Daogui returned to his native commandery and held himself high, often calling himself the emperor's uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Back home, Daogui gloried himself as the emperor's uncle.

sentences.zh: 數將儀衛，出入閭里，從故人游宴，庶僚鹹苦之。

translations.literal: He often took guards and attendants, going in and out of lanes, drinking with old friends; subordinates all suffered it.
translations.idiomatic: He paraded guards through the lanes and feasted with old friends; officials suffered it.

sentences.zh: 後郡廢，終於家，子孫無聞焉。

translations.literal: Later the commandery was abolished; he ended at home and his descendants are not heard of.
translations.idiomatic: When the commandery was abolished he died at home; no descendants are known.

sentences.zh: 論曰：三五哲王，防深慮遠；

translations.literal: The judgment says: The sage kings of the Three and Five dynasties guarded deeply and looked far ahead;
translations.idiomatic: The historian concludes: The sage kings of the Three and Five looked far and guarded deep;

sentences.zh: 舅甥之國，罕執鈞衡；

translations.literal: in states bound by uncle and nephew, few held the scales of power;
translations.idiomatic: among uncle-and-nephew realms, few kin ever held the balance;

sentences.zh: 母后之家，無聞傾敗。

translations.literal: among houses of empresses, one scarcely hears of ruin.
translations.idiomatic: in empresses' clans, collapse was scarcely heard of.

sentences.zh: 爰及漢晉，顛覆繼軌，皆由乎進不以禮，故其斃亦速。

translations.literal: By Han and Jin, overthrow followed in train—all because advancement ignored ritual, and so their fall came swiftly too.
translations.idiomatic: Come Han and Jin, ruin came in succession, for promotion without ritual brings swift destruction.

sentences.zh: 自魏至隋，時移四代，得失之跡，斯文可睹。

translations.literal: From Wei to Sui, four reigns passed; the traces of gain and loss lie plain in these pages.
translations.idiomatic: From Wei through Sui, four ages turned; their gains and losses are plain to read here.

sentences.zh: 苟不傾宗，終致亡國，周隋之際，可為鑒焉。

translations.literal: Even when a clan was not overthrown, the state was lost in the end—the Zhou and Sui interval may serve as a mirror.
translations.idiomatic: Even houses that did not fall by violence still lost the realm; the Zhou-Sui years are a mirror.

sentences.zh: 若使開皇創業，不取懲於已往，獨孤權侔呂、霍，必敗于仁壽之前；

translations.literal: Had Kaihuang's founding not taken warning from the past, and had Dugu's power rivaled Lü and Huo, he would surely have failed before Renshou;
translations.idiomatic: Had Wen of Sui not heeded the past, and Dugu Xin matched Lü and Huo in power, he would have perished before Renshou;

sentences.zh: 蕭氏勢均梁、竇，豈全于大業之後。

translations.literal: had the Xiao clan's power matched the houses of Liang and Dou, how could they have been preserved after Daye?
translations.idiomatic: had the Xiao house rivaled Liang Ji and Dou Xian, could it have outlasted Daye?

sentences.zh: 今或不隕舊基，或更隆先構，豈非處之以道，遠權之所致乎？

translations.literal: That some today do not fall from the old foundation, or again exalt what their forebears built—is this not because they were ruled by the Way and kept power at a distance?
translations.idiomatic: That some kin still stand, or rise again, comes of ruling by the Way and holding power at arm's length.
